Hearing impairment, interstitial nephritis, acute renal failure, abnormal liver function, dizziness & vertigo, convulsions, headache, somnolence. Cardiac disorders: palpitations, arrhythmia, supraventricular tachycardia, QT prolongation, torsades de pointes. Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders: allergic reactions, erythema multiforme, Steven-Johnson Syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs). NPRA Safety Alert (24 April 2025): Rare Risk of Cardiovascular Death.
drugs.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to azithromycin or any of the macrolides
drugs.interactions: Antacids. Ergot derivatives. Monitor patients on concurrent warfarin, digoxin or cyclosporin. Increase levels of tacrolimus, phenytoin, bromocriptine, disopyramide
drugs.precautions: Moderate or severe renal impairment; severe liver impairment; pregnancy & lactation
drugs.notes:
Frank Shann Drug Doses, 2017

  • Oral (only 40% bioavailable): 15 mg/kg (adult, 500 mg) on day 1 then 7.5 mg/kg (adult, 250 mg) days 2-5, or 15 mg/kg (adult, 500 mg) daily for 3 days; trachoma 20 mg/kg (adult, 1 g) wkly x3; MAC prophylaxis (adult) 1.2 g wkly; Gp A strep 20 mg/kg daily x3. IV: 15 mg/kg (adult, 500 mg) day 1, then 5 mg/kg (adult, 200 mg) daily. 1% eye drops: 1 drop 12 H for 2 days, then daily for 5 days.

Lexicomp, 2023

  • Susceptible infection
    • Infants, children and adolescents, 5 to 12 mg/kg/dose; typically administered as 10 to 12 mg/kg/dose on day 1 (usual maximum dose: 500 mg/dose) followed by 5 to 6 mg/kg once daily (usual maximum dose: 250 mg/dose) for remainder of treatment duration.
  • Cystic fibrosis; chronic lung maintenance
    • Limited data available; dosing regimen variable. Recommended for use in patients with a history of Pseudomonas aeruginosa; may also be considered in patients without Pseudomonas who experience frequent exacerbations. Patients should be screened for nontuberculous mycobacterial infection prior to treatment (if able) and azithromycin should not be used if present.
    • Weight-directed dosing: Infants ≥6 months, children and adolescents, 10 mg/kg/dose 3 times weekly; maximum dose: 500 mg/dose.
    • Fixed dosing: Children ≥6 years and adolescents
      • 18 to <36 kg, 250 mg 3 times weekly (Monday, Wednesday, Friday).
      • ≥36 kg, 500 mg 3 times weekly (Monday, Wednesday, Friday).
  • Bronchiectasis (noncystic fibrosis), prevention of pulmonary exacerbations (off-label use)
    • Adult, 500 mg 3 times weekly or 250 mg once daily. An initial dose of 250 mg 3 times weekly, with subsequent titration according to patient response, may be considered to minimize adverse effects.
    • Recommended for patients with ≥2 or ≥3 exacerbations per year; for those who do not have Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, have P. aeruginosa but cannot take an inhaled antibiotic, or continue to have exacerbations despite an inhaled antibiotic. Screen patients for nontuberculous mycobacterial infection prior to treatment, and azithromycin should not be given if present.
  • Travelers' diarrhea, empiric treatment
    • Most cases are self-limited and may not warrant antimicrobial therapy. Some experts reserve antimicrobial therapy for severe diarrhea (e.g. fever with blood, pus or mucus in stool) or certain high-risk travelers (e.g. those with an immunocompromising condition).
    • Adult, 1 g as a single dose or 500 mg once daily for 3 days. If symptoms have not resolved after 24 hours following single-dose therapy, continue with 500 mg once daily for 2 more days. A 3-day course of 500 mg once daily is the preferred regimen for dysentery or febrile diarrhea. Increased nausea may occur with the 1 g single-dose regimen, which may be reduced by administering azithromycin as 2 divided doses on the same day.

British National Formulary 86, 2023

  • Community-acquired pneumonia, low to moderate severity
    • Adult, 500 mg once daily for 3 days, alternatively initially 500 mg once daily for 1 day, then 250 mg once daily for 4 days.
  • Uncomplicated genital chlamydia; Uncomplicated non-gonococcal urethritis
    • Child 12-17 years (body-weight 45 kg and above), 1 g once daily for 1 day, then 500 mg once daily for 2 days.
    • Adult, 1 g once daily for 1 day, then 500 mg once daily for 2 days.
  • Uncomplicated gonorrhea
    • Adult, 2 g for 1 dose.
  • The macrolides have an antibacterial spectrum that is similar but not identical to that of penicillin; they are thus an alternative in penicillin-allergic patients. They are active against many-penicillin-resistant staphylococci, but some are now also resistant to the macrolides.
  • Azithromycin is a macrolide with slightly less activity than erythromycin against Gram-positive bacteria, but enhanced activity against some Gram-negative organisms including H. influenzae.
  • Plasma concentrations are very low, but tissue concentrations are much higher. It has a long tissue half-life and once daily dosage is recommended.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Treatment of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infection
    • HIV-negative adult, 250 mg once daily.
    • HIV-positive adult, 500-600 mg once daily.
    • HIV-positive child, 10 mg/kg (maximum 500 mg) once daily.
  • Primary prevention of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infection
    • Adult, 1.2 g taken once a week.
    • Child, 20 mg/kg (maximum 1.2 g) once a week or 5 mg/kg (maximum 250 mg) once daily.
  • Secondary prevention of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infection
    • Adult, 500-600 mg once daily.
    • Child, 5 mg/kg (maximum 250 mg) once daily.
  • Macrolides - Broad-spectrum antibacterials active against Gram-positive and some Gram-negative bacteria; also active against M. pneumoniae, Treponema pallidum, Bordetella pertussis, and Chlamydia, Chlamydophila, Legionella, Campylobacter and Borrelia spp. Macrolides are not active against enterococci.
  • Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis has been associated with use of azithromycin, particularly during the first 2 weeks of life; after this, the risk decreases, with no increased risk after 7 weeks of age. Risk is less than with erythromycin.
  • There is often cross-resistance between macrolides and lincosamides (clindamycin and lincomycin).

Product leaflet, accessed 2021

  • Binozyt 200 mg/5 ml Suspension
    • Shake the dry powder loose. For 15 ml (600 mg) bottle, add 8 ml water to the powder. Shake well until a homogenous suspension is achieved.
    • The prepared suspension can be kept at up to 30°C for 5 days.
  • Imexa 200 mg/5 ml Suspension
    • Shake to loosen powder. Add 9 ml of water to give 20 ml suspension. Shake vigorously to disperse powder.
    • For both powder and reconstituted suspension, keep container well closed, store below 30°C and protect from light. Use within 5 days after reconstitution.
  • Kidimac 200 mg/5 ml Suspension
    • Tap the bottle to loosen the powder. Slowly add boiled and cooled water up to the ring mark on bottle. Do not use tap water for reconstitution. Shake vigorously to mix medicine properly.
    • Before reconstitution, store below 30°C. After reconstitution, store the suspension at 25°C to 30°C. Reconstituted suspension should be used within 10 days. Discard the reconstituted suspension if more than 10 days. Do not freeze.
  • Zithrolide 200 mg/5 ml Suspension
    • Tap the bottle to loosen the powder. Add 8 ml of water to the bottle and shake well. Shake immediately prior to use.
    • Once reconstituted with water, the suspension has a shelf life of 5 days.
    • Dry powder (unopen bottle), store below 30°C. Once reconstituted with water, store in refrigerator at 2-8°C.
  • Zithromax 200 mg/5 ml Suspension
    • Tap the bottle to loosen the powder. Add water to the bottle (9 ml of water to the 600 mg bottle, 12 ml of water to the 900 mg bottle, 15 ml of water to the 1200 mg bottle, 19 ml of water to the 1500 mg bottle). Shake well. Shake immediately prior to use.
    • Store below 30°C for the powder and the reconstituted suspension. Shelf-life is 5 days for the reconstituted product.
  • Zithronam 200 mg/5 ml Suspension
    • Pack size 30ml: Tap the bottle to loosen the powder. Then add 20 ml of boiled and cooled water to the content of the bottle and shake well to mix uniformly. Shake immediately prior to use.
    • Pack size 50ml: Tap the bottle to loosen the powder. Then add 35 ml of boiled and cooled water to the content of the bottle and shake well to mix uniformly. Shake immediately prior to use.
    • Zithronam powder for oral suspension should be stored below 30°C. Protect from light and moisture.
    • After reconstitution the suspension should be stored below 30°C and be used within 5 days.
  • Zynomax 200 mg/5 ml Suspension
    • Tap the bottle to loosen the powder. Add 7 ml (for 15 ml) or 9 ml (for 20 ml) of water and shake well. Shake immediately prior to use.
    • Store below 30°C for powder reconstituted suspension. The reconstituted suspension form lasts up to 5 days.

(vi) Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis in pregnant patients with antibiotic allergy
(vii) Yaws (treatment & prophylaxis)

    • Active against Gram-negative aerobic organisms, e.g. Enterobacteriaceae, P. aeruginosa, (Gram-positive organisms and anaerobes are resistant); used as an alternative to aminoglycosides and broad-spectrum (anti-pseudomonal) cephalosporins.
    • More stable than cephalosporins to inducible AmpC beta-lactamases produced by some enteric Gram-negative organisms (ESCAPPM group) but, like all cephalosporins, is susceptible to extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) produced by some strains of Klebsiella and Enterobacter spp., E. coli and occasionally P. aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii.

drugs.indications:
i) Treatment of moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis in adult patients who have responded inadequately to, or who are intolerant to one or more disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs. May be used as monotherapy or in combination with methotrexate.
ii) Indicated for the treatment of severe atopic dermatitis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy.
iii) Treatment of severe alopecia areata in adult patients.
iv) Treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in paediatric patients 2 years of age and older who are candidates for systemic therapy.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions:
Indication i) Severe active rheumatoid arthritis: To be prescribed by Rheumatologist only.

Indication ii) Severe atopic dermatitis:
i. As fourth line of treatment in patients who have failed / have contraindications / experienced adverse events to:
- Intensive and optimized topical treatment
- Phototherapy
- At least two immunosuppressants
ii. To be prescribed by Dermatologists only.

Indication iii) Severe alopecia areata:
i. Reserved for patients who have demonstrated an inadequate therapeutic response, intolerance, or a documented contraindication to first-line conventional systemic therapies, which includes corticosteroids or non-targeted immunosuppressants.
ii. To be prescribed by Dermatologists only.

Indication iv) moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in pediatric patients:
i. As a fourth-line treatment for patients aged 2 to 11 years who have failed, have contraindications to, are unsuitable for, or have experienced adverse events from:
- Intensive and optimised topical treatment; AND
- Phototherapy; AND
- At least one conventional immunosuppressant.
ii. To be prescribed by Dermatologists or Paediatric Dermatologists only.
drugs.dosages:
Indication i) Severe active rheumatoid arthritis: 4 mg once daily.

Indication ii) Severe atopic dermatitis: The recommended dose of baricitinib is 4 mg once daily with or without food and may be taken at any time of the day. A dose of 2 mg once daily is appropriate for patients such as those aged ≥75 years and may be appropriate for patients with a history of chronic or recurrent infections. A dose of 2 mg once daily should be considered for patients who have achieved sustained control of disease activity with 4 mg once daily and are eligible for dose tapering. Baricitinib can be used with or without concomitant topical therapies (Refer package insert)

Indication iii) Severe alopecia areata: Administer 4 mg once daily, tapering to 2 mg for maintenance once sustained control is achieved. Initiate at 2 mg once daily for patients aged ≥65 years, those with chronic or recurrent infections, or those at elevated risk for VTE, MACE, or malignancy; this starting dose may be escalated to 4 mg if disease control remains inadequate.

Indication iv) moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in pediatric patients: The recommended dose of baricitinib is 4 mg once daily for patients weighing 30 kg or more. For patients weighing 10 kg to less than 30 kg, the recommended dose is 2 mg once daily.
drugs.adverseReactions: Upper respiratory tract infections, hypercholesterolemia, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, gastroenteritis, urinary tract infections, pneumonia, folliculitis, thrombocytosis >600 x 109 cells/L, headache, nausea, abdominal pain, ALT increased ≥3X upper limit normal (ULN), rash, acne, creatinine phosphokinase increased >5 x ULN.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the active substances, or to any of the other excipients.
drugs.interactions: Immunosuppressants such as azathioprine, tacrolimus or ciclosporin, probenecid, leflunomide, teriflunomide, ibuprofen, diclofenac.
drugs.precautions: Infections, tuberculosis, hematological abnormalities, viral reactivation, vaccination, lipids, hepatic transaminase elevations, malignancy, venous thromboembolism, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), immunosuppressive medicinal products, hypersensitivity, diverticulitis, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, elderly, women of childbearing potential, breast-feeding.
drugs.notes:
British National Formulary 85, 2023

  • Moderate-to-severe active rheumatoid arthritis (initiated by a specialist)
    • Adult 18-74 years, 4 mg once daily, for dose adjustments or treatment interruption due to side-effects, or dose reduction due to history of infection or sustained control of disease activity, consult product literature.
    • Adult 75 years and over, 2 mg once daily, for dose adjustments or treatment interruption due to side-effects, consult product literature.
  • Moderate-to-severe atopic eczema (initiated by a specialist)
    • Adult 18-74 years, 4 mg once daily, for dose adjustments or treatment interruption due to side-effects, or dose reduction due to history of infection or sustained control of disease activity, consult product literature. Consider discontinuation of treatment if no response after 8 weeks.
    • Adult 75 years and over, 2 mg once daily, for dose adjustments or treatment interruption due to side-effects, consult product literature. Consider discontinuation of treatment if no response after 8 weeks.
  • Manufacturer advises reduce dose to 2 mg once daily if creatinine clearance 30-60 ml/minute. Manufacturer advises avoid if creatinine clearance less than 30 ml/minute.
  • Clinical trial data have shown that baricitinib is associated with an increased frequency of venous thromboembolism (VTE) compared with placebo.
  • A European review of worldwide data concluded that baricitinib is associated with an increased risk of diverticulitis.
  • Manufacturer advises effective contraception during and for at least 1 week after treatment in women of child-bearing potential.

Lexicomp, 2023

  • Alopecia areata
    • Adult, initial: 2 mg once daily; if response is inadequate may increase to 4 mg once daily. For patients with nearly complete or complete scalp hair loss, with or without substantial eyelash or eyebrow hair loss, consider initiating therapy with 4 mg once daily. In patients receiving 4 mg once daily (as initial therapy or after a dose increase), reduce dose to 2 mg once daily once an adequate response is achieved.
    • Do not use in combination with other Janus kinase inhibitors, biologic immunomodulators, cyclosporine, or other potent immunosuppressants; do not initiate in patients with an absolute lymphocyte count <500 cells/mm3, ANC <1,000 cells/mm3, or Hb <8 g/dL.
  • Rheumatoid arthritis
    • Adult, 2 mg once daily.
    • For use as adjunctive therapy in patients who have not met treatment goals despite maximally tolerated methotrexate therapy; may also be used off-label as an alternative to methotrexate in disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD)-naive patients with moderate to high disease activity. Do not use in combination with biologic DMARDs or with strong immunosuppressants (e.g., azathioprine, cyclosporine); do not initiate in patients with an absolute lymphocyte count <500 cells/mm3, ANC <1000 cells/mm3, or Hb <8 g/dL.

Sanford Guide, 2021

  • COVID-19
    • Age 2 to <9 years, 2 mg once daily, with or without food.
    • Age ≥9 years and adult, 4 mg once daily, with or without food.
    • Duration of treatment: 14 days or until hospital discharge, whichever comes first.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Contact your doctor if you have persistent fever, itching or painful rash (shingles) or other signs of infection.
  • Live vaccines should not be given during treatment.

drugs.indications: Bendamustine is indicated for monotherapy in patients with indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphomas (iNHL) that has progressed during or within six months of treatment with rituximab or a rituximab-containing regimen.
drugs.dosages: Monotherapy for iNHL refractory to rituximab: 120 mg/m2 body surface area bendamustine hydrochloride on days 1 and 2; every 3 weeks.
drugs.adverseReactions: Hematological adverse reactions (leukopenia, thrombopenia), dermatologic toxicities (allergic reactions), constitutional symptoms (fever), gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting).
drugs.contraindications:
- Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients.
- During breast-feeding.
- Severe hepatic impairment (serum bilirubin >3.0 mg/dL).
- Jaundice.
- Severe bone marrow suppression and severe blood count alterations (leukocyte and/or platelet values dropped to <3000/µL or <75000/µL, respectively).
- Major surgery less than 30 days before start of treatment.
- Infections, especially involving leukocytopenia.
- Yellow fever vaccination.
drugs.interactions:
- Combination of bendamustine with cyclosporine or tacrolimus may result in excessive immunosuppression with risk of lymphoproliferation.
- Bendamustine metabolism involves cytochrome P450 (CYP) 1A2 isoenzyme. Therefore, the potential for interaction with CYP1A2 inhibitors such as fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin, acyclovir and cimetidine exists.
drugs.precautions: There are insufficient data from the use of bendamustine in pregnant women. In nonclinical studies bendamustine hydrochloride was embryo-/fetolethal, teratogenic and genotoxic. During pregnancy bendamustine should not be used unless clearly necessary. It is not known whether bendamustine passes into the breast milk, therefore, bendamustine is contraindicated during breastfeeding. Breastfeeding must be discontinued during treatment with bendamustine. No studies on the effects on the ability to drive and use machines have been performed. However, ataxia, peripheral neuropathy and somnolence have been reported during treatment with bendamustine. Patients should be instructed that if they experience these symptoms they should avoid potentially hazardous tasks such as driving and using machines. NPRA Safety Alert (6 Oct 2017): Increased Mortality Observed When Used in Non-approved Combination Treatments or Outside the Approved Indications.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • This medicine may increase your chances of getting an infection. Contact your doctor immediately if you develop a fever (temperature of 38°C or more) or any other signs of infection.
  • This medicine may also cause you to bruise and bleed more easily. Tell your doctor if unusual bruising or bleeding occur.
  • Tell your doctor or nurse if you have fever, chills, rash or itching. This is most likely to happen during, or within a few hours of, this treatment.
  • If a mild infusion-related reaction occurs, consider premedication with antihistamine, antipyretic and corticosteroid in subsequent cycles.
  • Alkylating agents may cause acute myeloid leukaemia, which usually occurs 3-8 years after treatment and is often preceded by myelodysplasia. Higher cumulative doses and combinations of alkylating agents increase the risk. Solid tumours can also occur.

British National Formulary 84, 2022

  • Use of bendamustine is associated with an increased incidence of acute leukemias.
  • Serious and fatal infections are reported, including opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP), varicella zoster virus (VZV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV). Manufacturer advises monitoring for respiratory signs and symptoms throughout treatment; patients should be advised to report new signs of infection, including fever or respiratory symptoms, promptly.
  • Reactivation of hepatitis B is reported in patients who are chronic carriers of the virus. Manufacturer advises monitoring for signs and symptoms of active hepatitis B during treatment and for several months after stopping treatment.
  • Evidence from clinical trials and a European review of safety data found an increased risk of non-melanoma skin cancers (basal and squamous cell carcinoma) in patients treated with bendamustine-containing regimens.
  • Effective contraception is required during treatment in men or women, and for 6 months after treatment in men.

drugs.indications:
Benralizumab is indicated as an add-on maintenance treatment in adult patients from 18 years with severe eosinophilic asthma characterized by the following criteria:
a) At least two exacerbations in the past 12 months on the current standard therapy (high-dose inhaled corticosteroids plus long-acting bronchodilators) and/or need for treatment with systemic corticosteroids.

drugs.interactions: None

drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Maintenance treatment for severe refractory eosinophilic asthma (add-on to optimised standard therapy)
    • Adult, child >12 years, SC 30 mg once every 4 weeks for the first 3 doses, then every 8 weeks.
  • Patients with baseline blood eosinophil count >300 cells/microlitre, or >150 cells/microlitre if taking oral corticosteroid, are most likely to benefit from treatment.

    • reduced exacerbations and improved lung function and asthma symptoms
    • allowed gradual reduction of oral corticosteroid dose; after 28 weeks of treatment 52% of patients taking benralizumab had stopped their oral corticosteroids and maintained asthma control, compared with 19% on placebo.

  • Benzalkonium chloride is a quaternary ammonium antiseptic and disinfectant with actions and uses similar to those of the other cationic surfactants (e.g. cetrimide). It is also used as an antimicrobial preservative for pharmaceutical products.

A 0.02 to 0.05% solution has been used as a vaginal douche. An aqueous solution containing 0.005 to 0.02% has been used for irrigation of the bladder and urethra and a 0.0025 to 0.005% solution for retention lavage of the bladder.
  • Creams containing benzalkonium chloride are used in the treatment of napkin rash and other dermatoses.
  • A 0.2 to 0.5% solution has been used as a shampoo in seborrheic dermatitis.
  • Solutions of 0.13% have been used for disinfection and storage of surgical instruments, sometimes with the addition of sodium nitrite to inhibit rust.

Product leaflet, accessed 2024

  • For the treatment and prevention of nappy rash redness. For the relief of nappy rash and for use as an adjunct to baby care hygiene for the prevention of nappy rash. For the aftercare of small areas of superficial burns (limited to the epidermis), limited sunburn and the effects of weather.
    • Adults (including the elderly), the affected area should be washed and dried thoroughly before applying Drapolene Cream. For optimum effect the area of application should be free from soap residue. A thin layer of cream should be applied evenly across the affected area several times a day, as necessary.
    • Neonates, infants and children, the nappy area should be washed then dried thoroughly at each change of nappy. For optimum effect the area of application should be free from soap residue. A thin layer of cream should be applied evenly across the affected area after every napkin change, paying particular attention to folds in the skin.
  • Do not use if you are allergic to benzalkonium chloride, cetrimide, lanolin or any of the other ingredients in this product.

Martindale The Complete Drug Reference, 2020

  • Benzalkonium chloride is a quaternary ammonium antiseptic and disinfectant with actions and uses similar to those of the other cationic surfactants (e.g. cetrimide). It is also used as an antimicrobial preservative for pharmaceutical products.
  • Cetrimide is a quaternary ammonium antiseptic with actions and uses typical of cationic surfactants. These surfactants dissociate in aqueous solution into a relatively large and complex cation that is responsible for the surface activity and a smaller inactive anion. In addition to emulsifying and detergent properties, quaternary ammonium compounds have bactericidal activity against Gram-positive and, at a higher concentration, against some Gram-negative bacteria. Some Pseudomonas spp. are particularly resistant as are strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. They are ineffective against bacterial spores, have variable antifungal activity, and are effective against some viruses.

  • Give by deep IM injection only in the upper, outer quadrant of the buttock or midlateral aspect of the thigh; avoid major nerves and blood vessels as severe neurovascular damage may occur.
  • Give doses >1.2 million units as 2 injections at separate sites.

drugs.notes:
Product leaflet, accessed 2020

  • Nixoderm ointment is used externally for pimples, blackheads, itching, rashes, ringworm of the skin and scalp.
  • Treatment for eczema, pimples and rashes
    • After cleansing, apply gently but thoroughly a liberal amount of Nixoderm ointment so that the entire surface is covered. This should be done twice daily, in the morning and evening. The treatment should be followed for seven days then discontinued for three days and resumed for further seven days. Continue this pattern of treatment until the condition has cleared up. If the skin problem persists after prolonged treatment, you should consult your doctor.
  • Treatment for foot itch
    • Clean and dry your feet thoroughly. Apply liberal amount of Nixoderm ointment onto the affected area, paying special attention to areas between the toes. This should be done twice daily, in the morning and evening. The treatment should be followed for seven days then discontinued for three days and resumed for further seven days. Continue this pattern until condition has cleared up. This is one of the most stubborn skin conditions, hence symptoms may disappear only to re-emerge. Therefore, it is recommended that treatment continue for three weeks after symptoms have disappeared.
  • Treatment for ringworm
    • Apply liberal amount of Nixoderm ointment twice daily, in the morning and evening. The treatment should be followed for seven days then discontinued for three days and resumed for further seven days. Continue this pattern until condition has cleared up. This is one of the most stubborn skin conditions, therefore it is recommended that treatment continue as long as it is necessary.

Lexicomp, 2024

  • General dosing, susceptible infection (non-CNS)
    • Infants, children and adolescents, IM, IV: 100,000 to 300,000 units/kg/day in divided doses every 4 to 6 hours; maximum daily dose: 24 million units/day.
  • Meningitis, including health care-associated ventriculitis/meningitis
    • Infants, children and adolescents, IV: 300,000 to 400,000 units/kg/day divided every 4 to 6 hours; maximum dose: 4 million units/dose; maximum daily dose: 24 million units/day.

    • CrCl <10 ml/min, 1-2 MU q4-6h.
    • HD, 1-2 MU q4-6h.
    • CVVH, 2 MU q4-6h.
    • CVVHD, 2-3 MU q4-6h.
    • CVVHDF, 2-4 MU q4-6h.

British National Formulary 88, 2024

  • Benzylpenicillin sodium (Penicillin G) remains an important and useful antibiotic but is inactivated by bacterial beta-lactamases. It is effective for many streptococcal (including pneumococcal), gonococcal, and meningococcal infections and also for anthrax, diphtheria, gas-gangrene, and leptospirosis.
  • Pneumococci, meningococci, and gonococci which have decreased sensitivity to penicillin have been isolated; benzylpenicillin sodium is no longer the drug of first choice for pneumococcal meningitis.
  • Benzylpenicillin is inactivated by gastric acid and absorption from the gastro-intestinal tract is low; therefore it must be given by injection.

  • Patients who are allergic to one penicillin will be allergic to all because the hypersensitivity is related to the basic penicillin structure.

drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Corticosteroids regulate gene expression, which results in:
    • glucocorticoid effects, e.g. gluconeogenesis, proteolysis, lipolysis, suppression of inflammation and immune responses
    • mineralocorticoid effects, e.g. hypertension, sodium and water retention, potassium loss.
  • Corticosteroids may have predominantly glucocorticoid effects (e.g. dexamethasone), mineralocorticoid effects (fludrocortisone), or a combination of both (e.g. hydrocortisone).
  • Take the tablets or oral liquid with food to help reduce stomach upset.
  • Tell your doctor immediately if you have any signs of infection.
  • This medication may affect your mood, e.g. you may feel more happy or sad than usual. It may also cause problems with sleeping; talk to your doctor if you have any concerns.
  • Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly unless your doctor tells you to. The dose may need to be reduced gradually when stopping treatment.
  • Tell all doctors, surgeons and dentists treating you that you are taking corticosteroids (or have taken them in the past) because if you become ill or are going to have surgery your dose of medicine may need to be increased.
  • Consider wearing a Medic Alert® bracelet and carrying a card with the details of your treatment.

drugs.indications: Topical corticosteroid indicated for the relief of inflammatory and pruritic manifestation of steroid-responsive dermatoses.
drugs.dosages: Apply sparingly to affected area 2 times daily then reduced to once daily when improvement occurs.
drugs.adverseReactions: Local skin atrophy, striae, systemic hypercorticism, folliculitis, hypertrichosis, acneiform eruptions, hypopigmentation and allergic contact dermatitis
drugs.contraindications: Viral diseases, bacteria and fungal infection, acne, rosacea and perioral dermatitis. Hypersensitivity to betamethasone products
drugs.interactions: Not known
drugs.precautions: Extensive or prolonged use, pregnancy, infant and children less than 4 years. Avoid contact with eyes
drugs.notes:
British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • Topical corticosteroid preparations should be applied no more frequently than twice daily; once daily is often sufficient.
  • Topical corticosteroids should be applied in sufficient quantity to cover the affected areas.
  • The length of cream or ointment expelled from a tube may be used to specify the quantity to be applied to a given area of skin. This length can be measured in terms of a fingertip unit (the distance from the tip of the adult index finger to the first crease). One fingertip unit (approximately 500 mg from a tube with a standard 5 mm diameter nozzle) is sufficient to cover an area that is twice that of the flat adult handprint (palm and fingers).
  • Several minutes should elapse between application of different preparations.
  • Potency
    • at 0.025%: moderate.
    • at 0.1%: potent
  • Patients and their carers should be reassured that side effects such as skin thinning and systemic effects rarely occur when topical corticosteroids are used appropriately.

Essential Practical Prescribing, 2016

  • Topical steroids range in potency from hydrocortisone (least potent), to Eumovate, Betnovate and Dermovate (most potent). Choice depends upon severity, site and the patient's age. It is important to remember that topical steroids are absorbed systemically and may also cause thinning of the skin. For this reason, it is important to use the appropriate strength depending on the site and severity of eczema and psoriasis.

  • Topical corticosteroid preparations should be applied no more frequently than twice daily; once daily is often sufficient.
  • Topical corticosteroids should be applied in sufficient quantity to cover the affected areas.
  • The length of cream or ointment expelled from a tube may be used to specify the quantity to be applied to a given area of skin. This length can be measured in terms of a fingertip unit (the distance from the tip of the adult index finger to the first crease). One fingertip unit (approximately 500 mg from a tube with a standard 5 mm diameter nozzle) is sufficient to cover an area that is twice that of the flat adult handprint (palm and fingers).
  • Several minutes should elapse between application of different preparations.
  • Potency
    • at 0.025%: moderate.
    • at 0.1%: potent
  • Patients and their carers should be reassured that side effects such as skin thinning and systemic effects rarely occur when topical corticosteroids are used appropriately.

Essential Practical Prescribing, 2016

  • Topical steroids range in potency from hydrocortisone (least potent), to Eumovate, Betnovate and Dermovate (most potent). Choice depends upon severity, site and the patient's age. It is important to remember that topical steroids are absorbed systemically and may also cause thinning of the skin. For this reason, it is important to use the appropriate strength depending on the site and severity of eczema and psoriasis.

drugs.genericName: Bilberry Extract (Fructus Vaccinium myrtillus Extract) 65 mg, Eyebright Extract (Herbs Euphrasia officinalis Extract) 65 mg, Wolfberry Extract (Fructus Lycium barbarum Extract) 45 mg, Marigold Extract (Flos Calendula officinalis Extract) 65 mg and Grape Seed Extract (Semen Vitis vinifera Extract) 45 mg Capsule
drugs.notes:
Product leaflet, accessed 2024 - Opceden

  • Opceden Bilberry EyeBright PLUS is an well rounded eye health formula which contains the most studied FloraGlo Lutein and other nutrients to support eye health.
    • Adult, take 1-2 capsules once daily, preferably taken after meal or as advised by the doctor/pharmacist.

The Review of Natural Products, 2024

  • There is a lack of consensus and limited evidence from clinical and epidemiological studies regarding whether an association exists between a higher intake of xanthophylls (lutein with or without zeaxanthin) and protection against age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and cataracts. Studies have also evaluated effects of lutein on cardiovascular outcomes. Clinical trial data are lacking to recommend use for any indication.
    • A dose of lutein 5 mg/day is widely accepted. AMD trials have used lutein dosages of 10 to 20 mg/day for varying durations (e.g., 4 to 12 months).
    • No clinically important adverse reactions were reported at lutein doses up to 20 mg/day.
  • Clinical trials have investigated use of bilberry for potential anti-inflammatory/anti-allergy, cardiovascular, and ophthalmic effects. However, clinical trial data are lacking to recommend use for any indication.
    • Clinical trial data are lacking to support specific dosing recommendations; studies are associated with limitations and often equivocal results.
    • One study evaluated bilberry extract 480 mg/day (treatment duration, 8 weeks) for mitigation of various symptoms of eye fatigue. Another similar study evaluated standardized bilberry extract 240 mg once daily for 12 weeks to improve ocular fatigue symptoms.
    • Typical bilberry products are standardized to 25% anthocyanoside content (approximately 36% anthocyanin), and 100 g of fresh fruit contains between 300 to 700 mg anthocyanin.
  • Eyebright preparations have been used to treat a variety of conditions, specifically inflammatory eye disease; however, clinical trial data are lacking to recommend use for any indication.
  • Two closely related species, L. barbarum and L. chinense, collectively produce the berries considered to be goji, wolfberries, or Gou Qi Zi.
    • Clinical data suggest antioxidant, CNS, antidiabetic, and ophthalmic effects.
    • A meta-analysis of 7 low-quality randomized controlled trials (N=548) suggested a reduction in cardiometabolic risk factors with supplementation for at least 3 months in healthy subjects at least 60 years of age.
    • However, limited quality clinical trials exist to support goji berry therapeutic claims.
  • Grape seed is known for its antioxidant properties. Studies suggest a possible role in cardiovascular disease. However, large quality clinical trials are lacking to recommend use for any indication.
    • Composition of commercial grape seed preparations is highly variable.
    • In clinical trials, grape seed extract has been studied for effects on various cardiovascular risk markers at oral doses of 150 to 2000 mg/day; formulations and durations of therapy (range, 2 to 24 weeks) varied.
    • In a safety and tolerability assessment in healthy Japanese adult volunteers, oral intake of grape seed extract up to 2500 mg for 4 weeks was found to be generally safe and well tolerated.

drugs.notes:
British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • Hypertension; Angina
    • Adult, 5-10 mg once daily; maximum 20 mg per day.
  • Adjunct in heart failure
    • Adult, initially 1.25 mg once daily for 1 week, dose to be taken in the morning, then increased if tolerated to 2.5 mg once daily for 1 week, then increased if tolerated to 3.75 mg once daily for 1week, then increased if tolerated to 5 mg once daily for 4 weeks, then increased if tolerated to 7.5 mg once daily for 4 weeks, then increased if tolerated to 10 mg once daily; maximum 10 mg per day.
  • Some beta-blockers are lipid soluble and some are water soluble. Water-soluble beta-blockers (such as atenolol, celiprolol hydrochloride, nadolol, and sotalol hydrochloride) are less likely to enter the brain, and may therefore cause less sleep disturbance and nightmares. Water-soluble beta-blockers are excreted by the kidneys and dosage reduction is often necessary in renal impairment.
  • Beta-blockers can precipitate bronchospasm and should therefore usually be avoided in patients with a history of asthma. When there is no suitable alternative, it may be necessary for a patient with well-controlled asthma, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (without significant reversible airways obstruction), to receive treatment with a beta-blocker for a co-existing condition (e.g. heart failure or following myocardial infarction). In this situation, a cardioselective beta-blocker should be selected and initiated at a low dose by a specialist; the patient should be closely monitored for adverse effects. Atenolol, bisoprolol fumarate, metoprolol tartrate, nebivolol, and (to a lesser extent) acebutolol, have less effect on the beta2 (bronchial) receptors and are, therefore, relatively cardioselective, but they are not cardiospecific. They have a lesser effect on airways resistance but are not free of this side-effect.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • This medicine may cause dizziness or tiredness especially at the start of treatment or when the dose is increased; if affected, do not drive or operate machinery.
  • If you feel dizzy, get up gradually from sitting or lying to minimize this effect; sit or lie down if you become dizzy.
  • Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly unless your doctor tells you to.
  • When stopping treatment, reduce dosage gradually, e.g. over at least 2 weeks; avoid abrupt withdrawal as it may exacerbate angina, or precipitate rebound hypertension, MI or arrhythmias.

  • Black seed also known as Habbatus Sauda by our locals is used for multiple purpose to maintain good health. It is considered as Makanan Sunnah by the Muslim community. The holy prophet Muhammed stated in his Hadith (teachings) 'Hold on to the use of the black seed for it has a remedy for every illness except death'. The research on its multiple health goodness is pretty extensive, primarily in the areas of cardiovascular health, inflammation, diabetes, fatty liver, obesity, kidney diseases, lungs protection, arthritis and skin protection. Black Seed is also an anti-inflammatory and reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines. It also modulates the immune system by increasing the macrophage population and stimulates the activity of these macrophages to engulf the foreign pathogens

The Review of Natural Products, 2024

  • Kalonji has been studied clinically for various uses, including dyspepsia, infertility, chronic kidney disease, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, obesity/overweight, and asthma. However, limited clinical studies exist to recommend use for any indication.
  • Various Nigella sativa dosages and dose forms have been evaluated in meta-analyses and controlled clinical trials.
    • Asthma: In a meta-analysis of high-quality randomized controlled trials, doses and dose forms of N. sativa varied and included 15 mg/kg/day of oil, 15 mL/kg of 0.1% extract, and 1 g/day of oil or crude plant; duration of interventions ranged from 4 weeks to 3 months.
    • Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: A meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials in adults with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease examined N. sativa supplementation doses ranging from 75 mg/day to 2 g/day (median duration, 12 weeks).
    • Obesity/overweight: N. sativa was assessed in the form of powder, oil, or extract of the seed according to pooled data from controlled clinical trials in patients who were overweight or with obesity. The dosage of the powder form varied from 1 to 2 g/day; the oil supplement dosage ranged from 3 to 5 g/day; and the extract was evaluated at 100 mg/day or 200 mg/day. The duration of interventions ranged from 6 to 12 weeks.
  • Information regarding safety and efficacy in pregnancy and lactation is lacking. Kalonji is reputedly an emmenagogue and a natural remedy for delayed menses; avoid during pregnancy. The seed has also been used traditionally as a lactagogue. Limited studies in the 1990s suggested that N. sativa oil might act as a contraceptive.

  • SubQ: Reconstitute each 3.5 mg vial with 1.4 ml NS to a concentration of 2.5 mg/ml. If injection site reaction occurs, the more dilute 1 mg/ml concentration may be used SubQ.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Compared to the IV route, the SC route has a lower incidence of peripheral neuropathy, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, fatigue and headache.
  • This medicine may increase your chances of getting an infection. Contact your doctor immediately if you develop a fever (temperature of 38°C or more) or any other signs of infection (including painful skin rash with blisters).
  • Tell your doctor if you have unusual bruising or bleeding or if you notice numbness or tingling in your fingers or toes.
  • You may feel dizzy or light-headed, especially when you stand up. To minimise this effect, get up slowly from sitting or lying and sit or lie down again if you feel dizzy. Follow instructions that you have been given to prevent dehydration and let your doctor know if you are affected by dizziness or fainting.
  • Peripheral neuropathy is usually sensory, affecting feet and hands; symptoms include pain, paraesthesias, burning dysesthesias and numbness. It is related to the cumulative dose and is the major dose-limitng effect, increasing in prevalence up to cycle 5. Symptoms usually improve or resolve if dose is reduced or treatment stopped. Autonomic neuropathy can also occur and may cause constipation, diarrhea, dizziness or orthostatic hypotension; motor neuropathy has also been reported.
  • Prophylaxis against herpes zoster is required.

  • The oleoresin gum from B. serrata has traditionally been used for its anti-inflammatory effects in conditions such as asthma, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, colitis, and irritable bowel syndrome. drugs.indications:
i. Treatment of adult patients with CD30+ Hodgkin Lymphoma (HL) at increased risk of relapse or progression following autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT).

ii. Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory CD30+ HL:
a. following autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) or
b. following at least two prior therapies when ASCT or multi-agent chemotherapy is not a treatment option.

iii. Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma (sALCL)
drugs.prescribingRestrictions:
Indications (i), (ii) & (iii): To be prescribed by Hematologist only
Indication (iii): Second-line therapy after failing one line of salvage therapy
drugs.dosages:
Indication i: The recommended dose is 1.8 mg/kg administered as an intravenous infusion over 30 minutes every 3 weeks. Brentuximab treatment should start following recovery from ASCT based on clinical judgment. These patients should receive up to 16 cycles.
Indication ii & iii: The recommended dose is 1.8 mg/kg administered as an intravenous infusion over 30 minutes every 3 weeks. The recommended starting dose for the retreatment of patients who have previously responded to treatment with brentuximab is 1.8 mg/kg administered as an intravenous infusion over 30 minutes every 3 weeks. Alternatively, treatment may be started at the last tolerated dose. Treatment should be continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients who achieve stable disease or better should receive a minimum of 8 cycles and up to a maximum of 16 cycles (approximately 1 year).

drugs.precautions: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy, pulmonary toxicity, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis, pancreatitis, serious infections and opportunistic infections, infusion-related reactions, peripheral neuropathy, hematological toxicities, tumor lysis syndrome, gastrointestinal complications, hepatotoxicity, use in pregnancy, hyperglycemia, sodium content in excipients.

drugs.genericName: Brinzolamide 1% and Brimonidine Tartrate 0.2% Ophthalmic Suspension
drugs.indications: Decrease of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in adult patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension for whom monotherapy provides insufficient IOP reduction.
drugs.dosages: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) 2 times daily.
drugs.adverseReactions: Ocular hyperemia, ocular allergic type reactions (eye allergy, keratitis, eye pain, ocular discomfort, blurred vision, abnormal vision, ocular hyperemia, conjunctival blanching), dysgeusia (bitter or unusual taste in the mouth following instillation) and dry mouth. The safety profile was similar to that of the individual components of brinzolamide 10 mg/ml and brimonidine 2 mg/ml.
drugs.contraindications:
- Hypersensitivity to the active substance(s) or to any of the excipients or to sulphonamides.
- Patients receiving monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitor therapy.
- Patients on antidepressants, which affect noradrenergic transmission (e.g. tricyclic antidepressants and mianserin).
- Patients with severe renal impairment.
- Patients with hyperchloremic acidosis.
- Neonates and infants under the age of 2 years.
drugs.interactions: It is contraindicated in patients receiving monoamine oxidase inhibitors and patients on anti depressants which affect noradrenergic transmission. Caution is advised in patients taking medicinal products which can affect the metabolism and uptake of circulating amines (e.g. chlorpromazine, methylphenidate, reserpine, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors), antihypertensives, cardiac glycosides, systemic medicinal products which may interact with α-adrenergic agonists or interfere with their activity i.e. agonists or antagonists of the adrenergic receptor (e.g. isoprenaline, prazosin), CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, clotrimazole, ritonavir and troleandomycin) and oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors concomitantly.
drugs.precautions: The medicinal product should not be injected. Patients should be instructed not to swallow the eye drops. Precaution on ocular effects, systemic effects, cardiac disorders, acid/base disturbances, hepatic impairment, mental alertness, the use of benzalkonium chloride and use in pediatric population.

  • Reduction of intraocular pressure (IOP)
    • Children ≥2 years and adult, instill 1 drop in affected eye(s) 3 times daily.

  • Discard 1 month after first opening.

drugs.indications: Indicated for the treatment of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions: For patients who require carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (CAI) but could not tolerate Dorzolamide.
drugs.dosages: 1 drop 2 times daily. Some patients may have a better response with one drop three times a day. The dose should not exceed 1 drop in the affected eye(s) 3 times daily.
drugs.adverseReactions: Blurred vision, eye irritation, eye pain, ocular discomfort, ocular hyperemia, dysgeusia
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or any of the excipients, severe renal impairment, hyperchloremic acidosis.
drugs.interactions:
- Acid-base disturbances have been reported with oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors. The potential for interactions (e.g. NSAIDS and Salicylates) must be considered in patients receiving Brinzolamide 1% ophthalmic suspension.
- There is a potential for an additive effect on the known systemic effects of carbonic anhydrase inhibition in patients receiving an oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitor and Brinzolamide 1% ophthalmic suspension. The concomitant administration of Brinzolamide 1% ophthalmic suspension and oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors is not recommended.
drugs.precautions: Hypersensitivity reactions that are attributed to sulphonamide may occur with Brinzolamide 1% ophthalmic solution as it is absorbed systemically. Acid-base disturbances have been reported with oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors. Use with caution in patients with risk of renal impairment because of the possible risk of metabolic acidosis. The possible role of brinzolamide on corneal endothelial function has not been investigated in patients with compromised corneas (particularly in patients with low endothelial cell count). Careful monitoring of patients with compromised corneas, such as patients with diabetes mellitus or corneal dystrophies, is recommended. Contains benzalkonium chloride which may cause eye irritation and is known to discolor soft contact lenses. Avoid contact with soft contact lenses. Temporary blurred vision or other visual disturbances may affect the ability to drive or use machines.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Your eye may feel uncomfortable for a little while after you have put in the drop. If you have blurred vision, avoid driving or operating machinery until your sight improves.

Product leaflet, accessed 2022

  • Discard 4 weeks after first opening.

Product website, accessed 2020 - VitaHealth

  • Each softgel contains broccoli extract (Brassica oleracea) 300 mg (providing sulforaphane 900 mcg).
  • Sulforaphane is a potent antioxidant which protects our bodily cells against oxidative stress. It is known to support the excretory system and prevent toxin build-up in the body.
    • Adults, take 2 softgels, once daily, after a meal or as recommended by a doctor or pharmacist.

The Review of Natural Products, 2020

  • Cruciferous vegetables, including broccoli, are being investigated for a potential role in the prevention and treatment of cancer, but no recommendations can be made. Preliminary data suggest broccoli sprout extract is hepatoprotective. Broccoli is a useful natural source of selenium.
    • Broccoli 500 g daily and broccoli sprouts 50 g daily have been used in clinical trials. Preparation methods affect bioavailability of active chemical compounds and relevant endogenous enzymes.
  • High consumption of broccoli may interfere with international normalized ratio (INR) values, antagonizing the effect of warfarin, but bioavailability of vitamin K is poor.

  • Manufacturer advises patients should be brought up-to-date with current immunisation schedule before initiating treatment.
  • Manufacturer advises that women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 12 weeks after stopping treatment.
  • Manufacturer advises store in a refrigerator (2-8°C) and protect from light.

drugs.indications:
i) Hypogonadism or Galactorrhea
ii) Acromegaly
drugs.dosages:
i) Initially 1-1.25 mg at bedtime increased gradually, usual dose: 7.5 mg daily in divided doses. Max 30 mg daily
ii) 1.25-2.5 mg at bedtime for 3 days and may be increased by 1.25-2.5 mg every 3-7 days up to 30 mg a day in divided doses
drugs.adverseReactions: Hypotension, peripheral vasoconstriction, dyskinesias, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, constipation, drowsiness, confusion, psychomotor excitation, hallucinations, dyskinesias, dryness of the mouth, leg cramps, allergic skin reactions. On prolonged treatment, reversible pallor of fingers and toes
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to bromocriptine products, toxemia of pregnancy, hypertension in postpartum and during puerperium
drugs.interactions: Clarithromycin - elevations in serum levels of bromocriptine. Inhibit ciclosporin metabolism. Erythromycin - significantly increase the bioavailability of bromocriptine. Bromocriptine, may decrease the metabolism of sirolimus, tacrolimus. Alcohol reduces tolerance to bromocriptine and vice-versa. Effects of antihypertensives may be potentiated. Avoid concurrent psychotropics
drugs.precautions: Nursing mothers, children under 15 years old, peptic ulcer disease, postpartum, puerperal women with high blood pressure, coronary artery disease, psychic disorders, concomitant use of other ergot alkaloid. Fertility may be restored (contraception needed), malignancy excluded before use for benign breast disease, acromegalic patients with history of peptic ulceration
drugs.notes:
Lexicomp, 2021

  • Neuroleptic malignant syndrome, moderate to severe (adjuvant agent) (off-label use)
    • Discontinue the causative agent(s) as soon as possible and provide aggressive supportive care throughout therapy.
    • Adult, initial: 2.5 mg every 8 to 12 hours; may increase to a maximum of 45 mg/day if needed. Continue therapy for ≥10 days, then taper slowly.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Ergot derivatives of dopamine agonist
    • Long-term use of high doses of ergot derivatives increases the risk of serious fibrotic adverse effects; they have largely been replaced by non-ergot derivatives in the treatment of Parkinson's disease.
    • Bromocriptine was the first dopamine agonist available and, due to extensive experience, it is the first-line drug in women with hyperprolactinemia wishing to conceive.
    • Cabergoline has a longer duration of action than bromocriptine and can be given once or twice weekly in hyperprolactinemia and once daily in Parkinson's disease. It is more effective and better tolerated than bromocriptine in hyperprolactinemia.
  • Daily doses should be taken at night, especially when starting treatment.
  • Take tablets with food to lessen the chance of nausea or stomach upset.
  • Tell your doctor if you develop shortness of breath, cough or chest pain.
  • Sometimes bromocriptine's side effects can be made worse by taking alcohol; avoid alcohol if this happens to you.

British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • Bromocriptine has been associated with pulmonary, retroperitoneal, and pericardial fibrotic reactions.
  • Treatment with dopamine-receptor agonists are associated with impulse control disorders, including pathological gambling, binge eating, and hypersexuality. Patients and their carers should be informed about the risk of impulse control disorders.
  • Excessive daytime sleepiness and sudden onset of sleep can occur with dopamine-receptor agonists. Patients starting treatment with these drugs should be warned of the risk and of the need to exercise caution when driving or operating machinery. Those who have experienced excessive sedation or sudden onset of sleep should refrain from driving or operating machines until these effects have stopped occurring. Management of excessive daytime sleepiness should focus on the identification of an underlying cause, such as depression or concomitant medication. Patients should be counselled on improving sleep behavior.
  • Hypotensive reactions can occur in some patients taking dopamine-receptor agonists; these can be particularly problematic during the first few days of treatment and care should be exercised when driving or operating machinery.

drugs.genericName: Budesonide 160 mcg and Formoterol 4.5 mcg Inhalation (Turbuhaler)
drugs.indications:
Prescriber category A/KK:
i) Regular treatment of asthma where use of a combination (inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta2-agonist) is appropriate:
- Patients not adequately controlled with inhaled corticosteroids and "as needed" inhaled short-acting beta2-agonists. or
- Patients already adequately controlled on both inhaled corticosteroids and long- acting beta2-agonists.
ii) As a reliever treatment for mild asthma patients who do not adhere to regular inhaled corticosteroid

Prescriber category A*:
iii) Treatment of COPD patients with a blood eosinophil count of 300 cells/microliter and more
iv) Treatment of COPD patients with blood eosinophil count of 100 cells/microliter and more with history of repeated exacerbation despite regular treatment with long-acting bronchodilators.
drugs.dosages:
i) Asthma maintenance therapy: Adult ≥18 yr, 160 mcg to 320 mcg BD. Some patients may require up to a max of 640 mcg BD. Adolescent 12-17 yr, 160 mcg to 320 mcg BD. Children 6-11 yr, 160 mcg BD, <6 yr, not recommended.
Maintenance & relief: Adult and adolescent ≥12 yr, 320 mcg/day either as 160 mcg BD or 320 mcg OD either morning or evening. For some patients a maintenance dose of 320 mcg BD may be appropriate. Patients should take 160 mcg additional inhalation as needed in response to symptoms. If symptoms persist after a few minutes, an additional inhalation should be taken. Not more than 960 mcg should be taken on any single occasion. A total daily dose of more than 1280 mcg is not normally needed, however a total daily dose of up to 1920 mcg could be used for a limited period. Patients using more than 1280 mcg daily should seek medical advice, should be reassessed & their maintenance therapy reconsidered.

ii) Asthma reliever-only therapy: 160 mcg as needed, but no more than 960 mcg to be taken on any single occasion. Children <12 yr, not recommended.

iii & iv) COPD: Adult ≥18 yr, 320 mcg BD.
drugs.adverseReactions: Palpitations, candida infections in the oropharynx, headache, tremor, mild irritation in the throat, coughing and hoarseness, tachycardia, nausea, muscle cramps, dizziness, agitation, restlessness, nervousness, sleep disturbances, bruises

drugs.precautions: Taper dose when discontinuing treatment. Seek medical advice if treatment is ineffective or exceeds highest recommended dose. drugs.notes:
Product leaflet, accessed 2024

  • Asthma reliever therapy (patients with mild disease)
    • Adults and adolescents 12 years and older, 1 inhalation as needed in response to symptoms. If symptoms persist after a few minutes, an additional inhalation should be taken. Not more than 6 inhalations should be taken on any single occasion. A total daily dose of more than 8 inhalations is normally not needed, however a total daily dose of up to 12 inhalations can be used temporarily. If the patient experiences a three-day period of deteriorating symptoms after taking additional as needed inhalation, the patient should be reassessed for alternative explanations of persisting symptoms.
    • Children under 12 years, not recommended.
  • Asthma reliever plus maintenance therapy
    • Adults and adolescents 12 years and older, the recommended maintenance dose of 2 inhalations per day should be given either as 1 inhalation in the morning and evening or as 2 inhalations in either the morning or evening. For some patients, a maintenance dose of 2 inhalations twice daily may be appropriate. The maintenance dose should be titrated to the lowest dose at which effective control of asthma is maintained.
    • Adults and adolescents 12 years and older, 1 additional inhalation as needed in response to symptoms to control asthma. If symptoms persist after a few minutes, an additional inhalation should be taken. Not more than 6 inhalations should be taken on any single occasion.
    • Adults and adolescents 12 years and older, a total daily dose of more than 8 inhalations is not normally needed; however, a total daily dose of up to 12 inhalations could be used for a limited period. If the patient experiences a three-day period of deteriorating symptoms after taking the appropriate maintenance therapy and additional as needed inhalation, the patient should be reassessed for alternative explanations of persisting symptoms.
    • Children under 12 years, not recommended.
  • Asthma maintenance therapy (fixed dose)
    • Adults 18 years and older, 1-2 inhalations twice daily. Some patients may require up to a maximum of 4 inhalations twice daily.
    • Adolescents 12-17 years, 1-2 inhalations twice daily.
  • COPD
    • Adults 18 years and older, 2 inhalations twice daily.

Sarawak Handbook of Medical Emergencies, 2019

  • IV loop diuretics produce immediate vasodilatation in addition to the more delayed diuretic response.

British National Formulary 92, 2026

  • Hypokalemia is dangerous in severe cardiovascular disease and in patients also being treated with cardiac glycosides. Often the use of potassium-sparing diuretics avoids the need to take potassium supplements.
  • In hepatic impairment, hypokalemia induced by loop diuretics may precipitate hepatic encephalopathy and coma - potassium-sparing diuretics can be used to prevent this. Diuretics can increase the risk of hypomagnesemia in in alcoholic cirrhosis, leading to arrhythmias.

drugs.adverseReactions: Light headedness, nervousness, apprehension, euphoria, confusion, drowsiness, tinnitus, blurred vision, diplopia, nausea, vomiting, sensations of heat, cold or numbness, urinary retention, paresthesia circumoral, hyperacusis, twitching, tremors, convulsions, unconsciousness, resp depression &/or arrest, agitation, numbness of the tongue, difficulty in swallowing & slurred speech. CV: bradycardia, hypotension: Hemodynamic: maternal hypotension. Neurologic: spinal block of varying magnitude (including total spinal block), hypotension secondary to spinal motor, sensory &/or autonomic (sphincter control) deficit of some lower spinal segment with slow recovery (several months) or incomplete recovery in rare instances when caudal or lumbar epidural block has been attempted. Backache & headache. Neuropathy, peripheral nerve injury & arachnoiditis. Inadvertent subarachnoid inj may lead to CNS depression, resp arrest & CV collapse. Allergic: cutaneous lesions, urticaria, edema or anaphylactoid reactions
drugs.contraindications: Allergy or hypersensitivity to amide type local anesth. Epidural or spinal anesth in patients with uncorrected hypotension. Infection and/or septicemia. Obstetric paracervical block, IV regional anesth (Bier's block). Thyrotoxicosis; regions with compromised blood supply, extremities. severe hemorrhage, severe hypotension or shock and arrhythmias, such as complete heart block, which severely restrict cardiac output (spinal anesthesia)
drugs.interactions: May potentiate the cardiac effects of antiarrhythmics (e.g. mexiletine & lignocaine). CNS acting drugs: tricyclic antidepressants or MAOIs, phenothiazines & butyrophenones. Oxytocic drugs of the ergot type. Adrenergic neuron blocking agents e.g. guanethidine, debrisoquine, bethanidine. β-blocker e.g. propranolol. Inhalation anesth e.g. chloroform, halothane, cyclopropane, trichloroethylene or other halogenated compounds. Cardiac glycosides, quinidine, hypoglycemics
drugs.precautions: Pre-existing neurological or neuromuscular disease e.g. myasthenia gravis; CNS or spinal cord disease e.g. meningitis, spinal fluid block, cranial or spinal hemorrhage, tumors, poliomyelitis, syphilis, TB or metastatic lesions of the spinal cord, severe hepatic disease, severe renal dysfunction, hyperthyroidism, epilepsy, severe bradycardia, severe cardiac conduction abnormalities, severe shock or digitalis intoxication, Stokes-Adams or Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, hypoxemia, acidosis, hyperkalemia, predisposition to malignant hypothermia, fetal bradycardia/tachycardia frequently follows paracervical block with some amide type local anesth & may be associated with fetal acidosis & hypoxia. Added risk in prematurity, toxemia of pregnancy & fetal distress. Monitor fetal heart rate. Pregnancy. Allergic type reactions including anaphylactic type symptoms & life-threatening or less severe asthmatic episodes in certain susceptible people. Extreme caution in patients with severe or untreated hypertension, poorly controlled thyrotoxicosis, ischemic heart disease, heart block, cerebrovascular insufficiency, advanced diabetes & any other pathological condition that might be aggravated by effects of adrenaline. Adrenaline may induce anginal pain in patients suffering from ischemic heart disease. Ventricular fibrillation, prefibrillatory rhythm, tachycardia, myocardial infarction, phenothiazine-induced circulatory collapse & prostatic hypertrophy

drugs.indications: Treatment of non-malignant pain of moderate intensity when an opioid is necessary for obtaining adequate analgesia. Not suitable for the treatment of acute pain.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions: For elderly patients or patients with comorbidities/difficult to swallow
drugs.dosages: Once weekly transdermal patch/for hospital use only. Patient aged 18 years and over, initial dose: 5 mcg/hr. For elderly: Renal impairment, No special dose adjustments necessary in patients with renal impairment; Hepatic impairment, Patients with hepatic insufficiency should be carefully monitored during the treatment with buprenorphine patch. Alternate therapy should be considered. Patch should be used with cautions in severe hepatic impairment patient
drugs.adverseReactions: Serious: respiratory depression & hypotension; Very common: headache, dizziness, somnolence, constipation, dry mouth, nausea, vomiting, pruritus, erythema; Common: anorexia, confusion, depression, insomnia, nervousness, anxiety, paresthesia, vasodilation, dyspnea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, rash, sweating, exanthema, tiredness, asthenia, pain, peripheral edema, application site reaction, erythema at site, chest pain.
drugs.contraindications: Patients with known hypersensitivity to the active substance of buprenorphine or to any of the excipients, treatment of opioid dependence & narcotic withdrawal. Conditions predisposing to severely impaired resp centre & function; myasthenia gravis; delirium tremens. Patients receiving MAOIs especially within the last 2 wk. Pregnancy & lactation
drugs.interactions: MAOIs; CNS depressants e.g. benzodiazepines; phenobarb, carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin; other opioids; certain antidepressants, sedative H1-receptor antagonists, anesth, alcohol, anxiolytics, neuroleptics, clonidine and related substances; CYP3A4 inhibitors.
drugs.precautions: Convulsive disorders, head injury, shock, reduced level of consciousness of uncertain origin, intracranial lesions, increased intracranial pressure, severe hepatic impairment; as analgesia in immediate post-op period. History of drug abuse. Avoid chronic use. May affect ability to drive or operate machinery. Patients <18 yr. NPRA Safety Alert (22 Jan 2026): Risk of Oesophageal Dysfunction.
drugs.notes:
British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • Prolonged use of opioid analgesics may lead to drug dependence and addiction, even at therapeutic doses. There is an increased risk in individuals with current or history of substance use disorder or mental health disorders.
  • Do not confuse the formulations of transdermal patches which are available as 72-hourly, 96-hourly and 7-day patches.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Patch is unsuitable for management of acute pain because it has prolonged onset and duration of action; rapid, safe dose titration is not possible
  • Write the date and time of application on the patch with permanent marker, then apply to dry, non-irritated, hairless skin on upper torso. Check the patch is still attached on the days between patch changes.
  • Remove after 7 days and put a new patch on a different area (avoid re-using the same area for at least 3 weeks).
  • When wearing the patch, do not allow it to come into contact with direct sources of heat such as electric blankets, heat pads, heat lamps, saunas or hot baths.

drugs.genericName: Buprenorphine HCl 2 mg and Naloxone HCl 0.5 mg Sublingual Tablet
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Opioid maintenance
    • Adult, 2-8 mg (of buprenorphine), depending on severity of withdrawal symptoms, in 1 or 2 doses on the first day. Increase daily dose by 2-8 mg every 1-3 days, depending on withdrawal symptoms and tolerance of adverse effects. Usual maintenance range, 12-24 mg daily (up to 32 mg daily).
    • Once stabilized, it may be possible to give up to double the usual daily dose (but no more than 32 mg) on alternate days.
  • Opioid withdrawal
    • Dose and length of treatment is tailored according to severity of withdrawal symptoms, as above, then dose is gradually reduced, e.g. over 5-8 days, to zero.
  • Place the tablets or films under the tongue until dissolved (takes 2-10 minutes).
  • It is possible that the first dose will cause some withdrawal symptoms (sometimes called precipitated withdrawal), but they are usually not severe. The symptoms may start within 1-4 hours and last for 2-5 days.
  • It may take a few days to find the most appropriate dose for you.
  • Buprenorphine may affect your ability to drive or operate machinery particularly when starting treatment, after the dose is increased or if you are taking other drugs.

drugs.notes:
Product leaflet, accessed 2026

  • Treatment of major depressive episodes
    • The recommended starting dose is 150 mg, given once daily. An optimal dose was not established in clinical studies. If no improvement is seen after 4 weeks treatment at 150 mg, the dose may be increased to 300 mg, given once daily. There should be an interval of at least 24 hours between successive doses.
    • The onset of action of bupropion has been noted 14 days after starting therapy. As with all antidepressants the full antidepressant effect of Zymon, may not be evident until after several weeks of treatment.
    • Patients with depression should be treated for a sufficient period of at least 6 months to ensure that they are free from symptoms.
  • Zymon should be swallowed whole. The tablets should not be cut, crushed or chewed as this may lead to an increased risk of adverse effects including seizures. Zymon can be taken with or without food.
  • Insomnia is a very common adverse event, which is often transient. Insomnia may be reduced by avoiding dosing at bedtime (provided there is at least 24 hours between doses).
  • Although no withdrawal symptoms were observed in clinical studies with bupropion, which were recorded spontaneously rather than systematically, a tapering therapy may be considered. Bupropion selectively inhibits the neuronal re uptake of catecholamines. A rebound effect or withdrawal symptoms cannot therefore be ruled out.
  • Zymon is not indicated for use in children or adolescents aged less than 18 years.The safety and efficacy of Zymon in patients under 18 years of age have not been established.

    • Adult, by subcutaneous injection, 200-500 micrograms once daily, increased if necessary up to 500 micrograms twice daily, starting in early follicular phase (day 1) or, after exclusion of pregnancy, in midluteal phase (day 21) and continued until down-regulation achieved (usually 1-3 weeks) then maintained during gonadotrophin administration (stopping gonadotrophin and buserelin on administration of chorionic gonadotrophin at appropriate stage of follicular development).

drugs.indications:
i) Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and other myeloproliferative diseases
ii) Haemopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT)

- refer to specific protocols
drugs.dosages:
i) Adult, initial: 2-4 mg daily. Maintenance: 0.5-2 mg daily. Stop when white blood cell less than 20 x 109/L. Child, 60 mcg/kg body weight daily
ii) Child, induction: 60 mcg/kg body weight daily (maximum 4 mg) if leucocytes more than 20,000/mm3 and platelets more than 100,000/mm3. Maintenance: 10-30 mcg/kg (maximum 2 mg daily)
drugs.adverseReactions: Myelosuppression, cataracts, hyperpigmentation, diffuse interstitial pulmonary fibrosis, gastrointestinal disturbances, veno-occlusive disease, gynecomastia, convulsions, impaired fertility and gonadal function, endocardial fibrosis, adrenal suppression, secondary malignancy
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to busulphan. Pregnancy and lactation
drugs.interactions: Itraconazole, paracetamol, live vaccines
drugs.precautions: Monitor blood counts during therapy. Caution in patients given radiotherapy or cytotoxic drug therapy recently
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Swallow tablets whole with a glass of water; do not break, crush or chew. Tell your doctor if you have difficulty in breathing or a persistent cough or bruising.
  • Myelosuppression
    • Low dose: pancytopenia may occur if treatment continues despite a large or rapid decrease in leucocyte or platelet count; pancytopenia can last from 1-24 months and is generally reversible.
    • High dose: causes profound myelosuppression; neutropenia occurs about 4 days after stem cell transplant with recovery 10-13 days later; thrombocytopenia occurs about 5-6 days after transplant.
  • An Addison-like syndrome (anorexia, vomiting, diarrhoea, weight loss, weakness, fatigue, hypotension, hyperpigmentation) has been reported following long-term treatment. Adrenal function usually remains normal. It may resolve after stopping busulfan.
  • Diffuse pulmonary fibrosis is usually insidious in onset, but may be acute. Presents as progressive difficulty in breathing and a persistent non-productive cough and fever. May be reversible if detected before clinical symptoms appear and the drug is stopped, but may progress to respiratory failure.

drugs.indications: For use in combination with cyclophosphamide as a conditioning regimen prior to allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for chronic myelogenous leukemia.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions: In selected cases with high risk of liver toxicity and intolerance to oral busulfan. To be prescribed by pediatric oncologist and consultant hematologist trained in transplant only.
drugs.dosages: 0.8 mg/kg of ideal body weight or actual body weight, whichever is lower via central venous catheter as a 2-hour infusion on the basis of every 6 hours for 4 days, for a total of 16 doses. For obese or severely obese patients, IV Busulfan should be administered based on adjusted ideal body weight
drugs.adverseReactions: Neurological toxicities: somnolence, lethargy and confusion. Seizure, gastrointestinal symptoms, anorexia, weight loss, weakness, hyperpigmentation, amenorrhea, cataracts, cough or hoarseness, impaired fertility and gonadal function, dry skin, liver damage, gynecomastia. Potentially Fatal: Bone marrow depression manifesting as thrombocytopenia, leucopoenia, anemia. Interstitial pulmonary fibrosis (known as "busulfan lung" on prolonged treatment).
drugs.contraindications: Busulfan is contraindicated in patients with a history of hypersensitivity to any of its components.
drugs.interactions: Decreased clearance when used with cyclophosphamide and itraconazole. Increased clearance by phenytoin. May reduce response to vaccines, possibility of generalized infections with live vaccines. Combination with thioguanine results in esophageal varices and abdominal liver function tests. Potentially Fatal: Cytotoxic agents may increase risk of pulmonary toxicity.
drugs.precautions: At the recommended dosage of busulfan injection, profound myelosuppression is universal, and can manifest as neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, or a combination thereof. Patients should be monitored for signs of local or systemic infection or bleeding. Their hematologic status should be evaluated frequently. Patients receiving busulfan should be monitored daily with a complete blood count and biochemistry (same as standard transplant protocol). Prior treatment with other myelosuppressive drugs, patients predisposed to seizures. May cause secondary malignancies (tumors, acute leukemias, ovarian failure). Previous irradiation/therapy. Discontinue if lung toxicity develops.

    • Do not apply the patch directly on skin.

  • Cooling gel sheet (single use medical device).
  • Features
    • Lasts up to 10 hours.
    • Gentle to skin.
    • Safe to use with medications.
  • Fever, headache, toothache and hot.
    • Remove the transparent plastic film and apply the adhesive side directly to the skin.

    • For external use only. Do not use on or around the eyes, on mucous membranes, or on skin affected by eczema, rashes or wounds.

    • Use the gel sheets promptly once the pouch is opened.
    • Use each gel sheet once only for efficacy and hygiene.
  • Other information
    • Keep unused gel sheets in the pouch.
    • Store in a cool dry place, away from direct sunlight.
    • Keep out of reach of children.
    • Fold the adhesive side of the used gel sheet in half and throw it away.

    • For external use only. Do not use on or around the eyes, on mucous membranes, or on skin affected by eczema, rashes or wounds.

    • The gel sheets should be used under the supervision of a parent or other adult, when used on a child or person who finds it difficult to use independently.
    • Do not cover the mouth or nose with the gel sheets.
    • Do not use for infants.
    • Clean the skin before applying the gel sheets.
    • Use the gel sheets promptly once the pouch is opened.
    • Use each gel sheet once only for efficacy and hygiene.

    • Keep unused gel sheets in the pouch.
    • Store in a cool dry place, away from direct sunlight.
    • Keep out of reach of children.
