  • Ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer, advanced, first-line maintenance therapy
    • Begin niraparib no later than 12 weeks following the most recent platinum-containing regimen; continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
    • Adult patient <77 kg or with a platelet count <150,000 mm3, 200 mg once daily.
    • Adult patient ≥77 kg and with a platelet count ≥150,000 mm3, 300 mg once daily.
  • Ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer, recurrent, germline BRCA mutated, maintenance treatment
    • Adult, 300 mg once daily, continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity or 200 to 300 mg once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Begin niraparib no later than 8 weeks following the most recent platinum-containing regimen.
  • Swallow whole; do not chew, crush or split.
  • Administer at approximately the same time each day, either with or without food.
  • If a dose is missed, administer the next dose at the regularly scheduled time. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not administer an additional dose.
  • Niraparib is associated with a moderate or high emetic potential; antiemetics are recommended to prevent nausea and vomiting. Consider administering at bedtime to diminish the potential for nausea and vomiting.

drugs.genericName: Nirmatrelvir 150 mg Tablet and Ritonavir 100 mg Tablet
drugs.notes:
Sanford Guide, 2021

  • Treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 disease, and who are at high risk of progression to severe COVID-19, including hospitalization or death.
    • Adult (age ≥12 years and weight ≥40 kg), nirmatrelvir 300 mg twice daily and ritonavir 100 mg twice daily (taken together, with or without food) for five days.
    • eGFR ≥30 to <60 ml/min, nirmatrelvir 150 mg BD and ritonavir 100 mg BD, both for 5 days.
    • eGFR <30 ml/min, not recommended (no data).
  • Initiate treatment as soon as possible after COVID-19 diagnosis, and within five days of symptom onset.

drugs.genericName: Nirsevimab 100 mg/1 ml Solution for Injection in Pre-filled Syringe
drugs.indications:
Indicated for the prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in:
i. Neonates and infants during their first RSV season.
ii. Children up to 24 months of age who remain vulnerable to severe RSV disease through their second RSV season.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions:
i. Infants at high risk, including those with:
- Prematurity: born at ≤32 weeks gestational age.
- Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) or chronic lung disease (CLD)
- Congenital heart disease (CHD)
- Immunocompromised (immunodeficiency)

ii. Not indicated for neonates and young infants <6 months of age whose mothers received an RSV vaccine during the third trimester at least 14 days before delivery, as maternal vaccination is expected to provide passive protection against severe RSV disease.

iii. To be prescribed by Neonatologists, Paediatric Infectious Disease and Paediatric Cardiologists only.
drugs.dosages:
First RSV season:
i. Body weight <5kg, 50 mg intramuscularly.
ii. Body weight ≥5kg, 100 mg intramuscularly.
Second RSV season: 200 mg intramuscularly.

Refer to package insert for full details on dose for specific population or condition.
drugs.adverseReactions: Hypersensitivity, rash, pyrexia and injection site reactions.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to nirsevimab or to any of the excipients (L-histidine, L-histidine hydrochloride, L-arginine hydrochloride, sucrose, polysorbate 80 (E433) and water for injections).
drugs.interactions: None
drugs.precautions: Hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis, clinically significant bleeding disorders, immunocompromised children and allergic to polysorbate 80 (E433).
drugs.notes:
Lexicomp, 2024

  • Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), prevention
    • Administer shortly before the RSV season begins; if not administered before start of season, may administer at any time during the season.
    • Patient's first RSV season
      • While nirsevimab is FDA approved for all infants in their first RSV season, ACIP and AAP recommendations specify use in infants <8 months of age.
      • Infants weight <5 kg, IM: 50 mg as a single dose.
        • Patients who undergo cardiopulmonary bypass after dose: IM: Administer a 50 mg dose as soon as patient is stable after surgery (regardless of time elapsed).
      • Infants weight ≥5 kg, IM: 100 mg as a single dose.
        • Patients who undergo cardiopulmonary bypass after dose: Administer an additional dose as follows as soon as patient is stable after surgery:
          • ≤90 days since initial dose: IM: 100 mg as a single dose.
          • >90 days since initial dose: IM: 50 mg as a single dose.
    • Patient's second RSV season
      • While nirsevimab is FDA approved for patients up to 24 months of age who remain at increased risk for severe disease during their second RSV season, ACIP and AAP recommend second-season dosing only for patients 8 to ≤19 months of age who are at increased risk for severe disease (Ref).
      • Infants and Children <24 months, IM: 200 mg as a single dose.
        • Patients who undergo cardiopulmonary bypass after dose: Administer an additional dose as follows as soon as patient is stable after surgery:
          • ≤90 days since initial dose: IM: 200 mg as a single dose.
          • >90 days since initial dose: IM: 100 mg as a single dose.
  • Store intact vials between 2°C to 8°C in original carton to protect from light. May be kept at 20°C to 25°C for a maximum of 8 hours. After removal from the refrigerator, must be used within 8 hours or discarded. Do not freeze, shake, or expose to heat.

drugs.indications:
i) Acromegaly treatment in patients in whom surgery or radiotherapy is inappropriate or ineffective- based on level of growth hormone and high IGF-1 and residual pituitary tumor
ii) Relief of symptoms associated with functional gastro-entero-pancreatic (GEP) endocrine tumors: - Carcinoid tumors with features of the carcinoid syndrome.
- VIPomas, Glucagonomas
- Gastrinomas/Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
- Insulinomas
- GRFomas.
iii) Prevention of complications following pancreatic surgery
iv) Emergency management of bleeding gastro-esophageal varices in patients with cirrhosis
drugs.dosages:
i) Initially 0.05-0.1 mg SC every 8 or 12 hours. Optimal daily dose is 0.3 mg, not to exceed maximum dose of 1.5 mg/day.
ii) Initially 0.05 mg once or twice daily, gradually increase to 0.1-0.2 mg 3 times daily. Higher doses may be required in exceptional circumstances.

The dosing is individualized according to product insert/protocol.
drugs.adverseReactions: Anorexia, nausea, vomiting, crampy abdominal pain, abdominal bloating, flatulence, loose stools, diarrhea, and steatorrhea. drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to octreotide
drugs.interactions: Reduces absorption of cyclosporin and to delay that of cimetidine. Concomitant of octreotide and bromocriptine increase the availability of bromocriptine.
drugs.precautions: Growth hormone secreting pituitary tumors (can expand and cause space occupying effects), insulinomas (exaggerate hypoglycemia), diabetes, pregnancy and lactation

drugs.notes:
Lexicomp, 2024

  • A low starting dose (e.g. 2.5 mg) and more gradual titration may be better tolerated in patients who are medically ill, at risk for postural hypotension, or may metabolize more slowly (e.g. nonsmoking, female, ≥65 years of age).
  • Due to the drug's sedating effect, bedtime dosing is preferred; alternatively, divided doses may improve tolerability.
  • Agitation/Aggression and psychosis associated with dementia, severe or refractory (alternative agent) (off-label use)
    • Patients with dementia with Lewy bodies are at increased risk for severe adverse reactions; caution is required even with low doses.
    • Adult, oral: Initial: 2.5 mg once daily, may increase dose based on response and tolerability in increments of 2.5 to 5 mg/day at intervals ≥1 week up to 10 mg/day. In patients without a clinically significant response after an adequate trial (eg, up to 4 weeks), taper and withdraw therapy. Only continue in patients with demonstrated benefit; attempt to taper and withdraw at regular intervals (eg, within 4 months of initiation).
  • Cancer-related anorexia and cachexia (off-label use)
    • In the study, all randomized patients had received antiemetic prophylaxis with olanzapine 5 mg once daily for 4 days plus dexamethasone during/following each cycle of chemotherapy, followed by low-dose olanzapine for cancer-related anorexia.
    • Adult, 2.5 mg once daily for 12 weeks.
  • Chemotherapy-induced acute and delayed nausea or vomiting (high emetic risk [>90%]), prevention (off-label use)
    • Adult, 5 or 10 mg on day of chemotherapy (day 1), followed by 5 or 10 mg once daily on days 2 to 4, in combination with antiemetics used for high emetic risk agents. For cisplatin-based high emetic-risk therapy, the 5 mg (in combination with triple antiemetic therapy) is effective and may be associated with less daytime sedation.
  • Chemotherapy-induced breakthrough nausea or vomiting, treatment (off-label use)
    • Adult, 5 to 10 mg once daily for 3 days.
  • Nausea and vomiting (persistent) associated with advanced cancer (off-label use)
    • Adult, 5 mg once daily for 7 days; treatment may be continued beyond 7 days if clinically beneficial.

ACCP Updates in Therapeutics, 2023

  • Olanzapine is structurally similar to clozapine and has a similar pharmacologic profile. Unlike clozapine, it does not require strict monitoring for agranulocytosis.
  • Together with clozapine, olanzapine carries the highest risk of diabetes. For this reason, many schizophrenia treatment guidelines do not consider it first-line therapy.

British National Formulary 87, 2024

  • Manufacturer advises olanzapine orodispersible tablet may be placed on the tongue and allowed to dissolve, or dispersed in water, orange juice, apple juice, milk, or coffee

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Tell your doctor if you start or stop smoking tobacco, as your dose may need to be changed.
  • Response to oral route may occur in 1-2 weeks; allow 2-3 months for full trial.
  • It is possible to overlap drugs when switching from another antipsychotic provided there is close supervision and monitoring.
  • After stopping long-acting antipsychotic injection, start oral olanzapine at scheduled time of next injection
  • Use wafer or orally disintegrating tablet for acutely psychotic patients, those who have difficulty swallowing, or to help ensure compliance.
  • Taking your antipsychotic medicine regularly is important:
    • because stopping or taking it irregularly is associated with high risk of relapse and suicide.
    • in order to prevent an episode, rather than taking it after symptoms occur.
  • This medicine may cause drowsiness and may increase the effects of alcohol, cannabis or sleeping tablets. Do not drive or operate machinery if you are affected.
  • You may feel dizzy on standing when taking this medicine. Get up gradually from sitting or lying to minimise this; sit or lie down if you become dizzy.

drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Hypertension
    • Adult, initially 20 mg once daily; after 8 weeks, increase if necessary to 40 mg once daily.
    • Child,
      • 1-6 years, initially 0.3 mg/kg (maximum 10 mg) once daily; after 2 weeks, increase if necessary to a maximum of 0.6 mg/kg (not to exceed 20 mg once daily)
      • >6 years, 20-35 kg, initially 10 mg once daily; after 2 weeks, increase if necessary to a maximum of 20 mg once daily.
      • >6 years, >35 kg, initially 20 mg once daily; after 2 weeks, increase if necessary to a maximum of 40 mg once daily.
  • Contraindicated if CrCl is <30 ml/minute, biliary obstruction (partly eliminated in bile) or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 10-15).
  • Tell your doctor if you have severe or chronic diarrhoea.
  • You may feel dizzy when you start taking this medicine. Get up gradually from sitting or lying to minimise this effect; sit or lie down if you become dizzy or light-headed.
  • When starting a sartan:
    • stop potassium supplements and potassium-sparing diuretics
    • in heart failure, consider reducing dose or withholding other diuretics for 24 hours before starting a sartan
    • review use of NSAIDs (including selective COX‑2 inhibitors)
    • start with a low dose
  • Check renal function and electrolytes before starting a sartan and review after 1-2 weeks.
  • Unlike ACE inhibitors, sartans do not inhibit the breakdown of bradykinin and may be useful if an ACE inhibitor is not tolerated because they:
    • cause less cough than ACE inhibitors
    • may be used if there is a history of angioedema caused by an ACE inhibitor (with close monitoring as there is a small risk of recurrence)
  • Maximum antihypertensive effect occurs about 4-6 weeks after starting treatment.

ACCP Updates in Therapeutics, 2021

  • ACEIs and ARBs exerts a predictable dose-related reduction in GFR. SCr is usually expected to increase by up to 30%. It usually occurs within 2-5 days and stabilizes in 2-3 weeks. Increases greater than 30% may be harmful. It is usually reversible on drug discontinuation.

British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • Angiotensin-II receptor antagonists should be avoided in pregnancy unless essential. They may adversely affect foetal and neonatal blood pressure control and renal function; neonatal skull defects and oligohydramnios have also been reported.

drugs.genericName: Omalizumab 150 mg Powder and Solvent for Solution
drugs.indications:
i) For adults and adolescents (≥12 years), for severe persistent allergic asthma whose symptoms are inadequately controlled with inhaled corticosteroids;
ii) For children (6 to <12 years of age): As add-on therapy to improve asthma control with severe persistent allergic asthma who have positive skin test or in vitro reactivity to a perennial aero allergen and frequent daytime symptoms or night-time awakenings and who have had multiple documented severe asthma exacerbations despite daily high-dose inhaled corticosteroids, plus a long-acting inhaled beta2 agonist
drugs.dosages:
i) Adult & adolescent ≥12 yr, 150-375 mg SC every 2-4 wk, according to body wt & baseline serum total IgE level.. For subcutaneous administration only. Do not administer by the intravenous or intramuscular route.
ii) Appropriate dose and dosing frequency of omalizumab is determined by baseline IgE (IU/ml), measured before the start of treatment, and body weight (kg). Prior to initial dosing, patients should have their IgE level determined for their dose assignment. Based on these measurements 150-375 mg in 1-3 injections may be needed for each administration. Patients whose baseline IgE levels or body weight in kilograms are outside the limits of the dosing table should not be given omalizumab. For subcutaneous administration only.
drugs.adverseReactions: Injection site pain, swelling, erythema, pruritis, headache. Anaphylactic reactions, allergic conditions, allergic bronchospasm
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to omalizumab or to any of the excipients
drugs.interactions: No significant interaction observed in clinical trials
drugs.precautions: Not for treatment of acute asthma exacerbations, acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus. Renal or hepatic impairment, DM, glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome, fructose intolerance or sucrose-isomaltase deficiency. Pregnancy & lactation.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Asthma
    • Adult, child >6 years, SC 75-375 mg every 2-4 weeks (maximum 150 mg per injection site). Dose is based on weight and baseline serum total IgE level. Continue inhaled corticosteroid (consider reducing the corticosteroid dose after 4 months of combined treatment).
    • Most clinical trials included patients with raised baseline serum total IgE levels (30-700 IU/mL for adults; 30-1300 IU/mL for children <12 years) and a positive skin test to at least 1 allergen.
    • Increased rates of arterial thrombotic events have been reported with omalizumab use in clinical trials and an observational study; further epidemiological studies are required to quantify this risk.
  • Chronic spontaneous urticaria
    • Adult, child>12 years, SC 300 mg every 4 weeks (maximum 150 mg per injection site). Continue regular antihistamine treatment.
    • Clinical trials were short (maximum of 6 months). In these trials, 150 mg every 4 weeks was adequate for some patients.

MIMS, 2022

  • Store at 2-8°C (in a refrigerator). Do not freeze. Store in the original package.

  • May be taken with food to avoid gastrointestinal disturbances.

The Review of Natural Products, 2021

  • The AHA recommends a minimum of 2 fatty fish servings per week. Clinical trials suggest fish oil supplementation of omega-3 fatty acid 1 g/day in coronary heart disease, and when triglycerides are elevated, a minimum of omega-3 fatty acid 2 g/day, up to a maximum of 4 g/day. Fish oil supplements generally contain 1000 mg of fish oil, which approximates to 300 to 400 mg of EPA and DHA.
  • Emulsified oral preparations have been developed to improve the taste over encapsulated fish oils and may increase digestion and absorption of the fatty acids via modifications in solubility. Encapsulated oils have been found to oxidize and become rancid over time and with processing method, which may have an effect on total EPA/DHA delivered.

drugs.indications:

Frank Shann Drug Doses, 2017

  • Usually 0.4-0.8 mg/kg (adult, 20-40 mg) 12-24 H oral. ZE synd: 1 mg/kg (adult, 60 mg) 12-24 H oral, incr up to 3 mg/kg (adult, 120 mg) 8 H if reqd.

Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics, 2019

  • All PPIs are most effective if taken about 30 minutes before a meal because they inhibit only actively secreting proton pumps, and meals are the main stimulus of proton pump activity.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Swallow tablet or capsule whole, do not crush or chew. You can disperse omeprazole tablets (Losec®, Acimax®, Omepral®) in water, orange juice or yoghurt and take within 30 minutes.
  • All PPIs have similar efficacy and adverse effects, although they may differ in their potential to cause drug interactions.
  • Tell your doctor if you develop symptoms such as black stools or vomit that looks like coffee grounds.
  • Assess ongoing PPI use regularly; if symptoms are well controlled (after at least 4-8 weeks of treatment), consider:
    • stopping treatment (unless patient has severe oesophagitis or complicated disease, e.g. Barrett's, high risk of GI bleeding)
    • intermittent use when symptoms develop
    • step down to low-dose therapy
  • Enteric infections (including Clostridium difficile-associated disease) have been associated with PPI sue (observational data).
  • Although data are conflicting, some observational studies suggest possible associations between long-term PPI therapy and decreased serum vitamin B12 concentration, pneumonia, fracture, iron deficiency and chronic kidney disease.

drugs.genericName: Onasemnogene Abeparvovec 2 x 10^13 vg/ml Suspension for Intravenous Infusion
drugs.notes:
Lexicomp, 2024

  • Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA)
    • Infants and children <2 years, IV infusion: 1.1 x 1014 vector genomes/kg as a single dose.
  • Beginning the day prior to onasemnogene abeparvovec infusion, oral corticosteroid (prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day or equivalent) should be administered and continued for ≥30 days to help prevent hepatic toxicity. At the end of 30 days, clinically assess liver status and check LFTs (ALT, AST, total bilirubin, PT, and INR) and manage as follows:
    • If unremarkable findings (normal clinical exam, total bilirubin, PT, INR, and ALT and AST concentrations <2 × ULN), taper corticosteroid over 28 days; do not discontinue abruptly.
    • If evidence of liver function abnormalities exists, continue oral corticosteroid (prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day or equivalent) until AST and ALT <2 × ULN and all other assessments return to normal, then taper corticosteroid over 28 days or longer if needed; do not discontinue abruptly.
    • If liver function abnormalities persist ≥2 × ULN after 30 days of corticosteroid therapy, consult pediatric gastroenterologist or hepatologist.
  • Cases of acute liver failure with fatal outcomes have been reported. Acute serious liver injury and elevated aminotransferases can occur with onasemnogene abeparvovec. Patients with preexisting liver impairment may be at higher risk. Prior to infusion, assess liver function of all patients by clinical examination and laboratory testing. Administer systemic corticosteroid to all patients before and after onasemnogene abeparvovec infusion. Continue to monitor liver function for at least 3 months after infusion and at other times as clinically indicated.
  • Product is shipped and delivered frozen at ≤60°C. Upon receipt, store at 2-8°C for ≤14 days. Do not refreeze.

drugs.indications:
i) Prevention of nausea and vomiting induced by chemotherapy and radiotherapy
ii) Postoperative nausea and vomiting
drugs.dosages:
i) 8 mg given by IV infusion over 15 minutes or by IM immediately before treatment followed by 8 mg orally every 12 hours for up to 5 days. Child, 5 mg/m2 body surface IV over 15 minutes immediately before chemotherapy followed by 4 mg orally every 12 hours for up to 5 days
ii) Prevention: 4 mg given by IV at induction of anesthesia. Child over 2 years, 100 mcg/kg (max 4 mg) by slow IV before, during or after induction of anesthesia.
Treatment of postoperative: 4 mg by IM or slow. Child over 2 years, 100 mcg/kg (maximum 4 mg) by slow IV
drugs.adverseReactions: Headache, malaise, fatigue, sedation, diarrhea, constipation, anaphylaxis sensation of flushing or warmth in the head and epigastrium, occasionally transient visual disturbances and dizziness, involuntary movements, seizures and arrhythmias
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to any component of the preparation or other selective 5-HT3 antagonists
drugs.interactions: In patients treated with potent inducers of CYP3A4 (i.e., phenytoin, carbamazepine and rifampicin), the oral clearance of ondansetron was increased and ondansetron blood concentrations were decreased. Ondansetron may reduce the analgesic effect of tramadol
drugs.precautions: Pregnancy, lactation, hepatic impairment. May mask progressive ileus and/or gastric distension. NPRA Safety Alert (30 Apr 2014): Dose-dependent QT interval prolongation.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • All 5HT3 antagonists appear similarly effective; however, compared to ondansetron, palonosetron is more effective in preventing postoperative vomiting.
  • Granisetron and tropisetron are given once daily (children may need tropisetron twice daily postoperatively); ondansetron is given 2 or 3 times daily. Palonosetron is given as a single dose due to its long half-life of approximately 40 hours (>100 hours in about 10% of the population).
  • 5HT3 antagonists may be used for nausea and vomiting if other drugs are inadequate. If used, ondansetron is preferred because of greater experience; limited data for granisetron (human data lacking for tropisetron and palonosetron). There are conflicting data about the association of ondansetron, used in the first trimester, with a small increased risk of malformations, e.g. orofacial clefts.

drugs.brandName: ORS B Plus, ORS Plus, N-ORS, UphaLyte
drugs.indications: Replacement of fluid and electrolytes loss in diarrhea
drugs.dosages:
Dissolve 1 sachet in 200 or 250 ml of water according to product insert. The amount to give depends on hydration status.

Adult, 200-400 ml (1-2 sachets) for every loose motion / diarrhea / vomiting. Child 2 years & above, 100-200 ml (1 sachet) for every loose motion / diarrhea / vomiting. In severe dehydration, 100 ml/kg for 3-4 hours. Infant up to 2 years, 1-1.5 times their usual feed volume (50-100 ml) each diarrhea/vomiting.

Dose is according to product insert and dependent on the product / brand used as well as patient comorbidities e.g. heart failure and chronic kidney disease.
drugs.adverseReactions: Hypernatremia, nausea and vomiting
drugs.contraindications: Patients with renal failure or hyperkalemia
drugs.interactions: Potassium sparing diuretics
drugs.precautions: Cardiac failure, hypertension, impaired renal function, peripheral and pulmonary edema, toxemia in pregnancy
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Follow directions on label for reconstitution, and dose according to severity of diarrhea and weight or age of patient.

Product leaflet, accessed 2021

  • N-ORS
    • Each sachet contains sodium chloride 658 mg, potassium chloride 375 mg, sodium citrate 735 mg and glucose anhydrous 3382 mg. Ionic concentration (mmol/litre): Na+ 75, K+ 20, Cl- 65, citrate 10 and glucose 75.
    • For cases of hypotonic dehydration resulting from diarrhea, vomiting and physical exertion.
      • Dissolve contents in 250 ml of boiled, cool water and to be taken orally. Unused solution should be stored in a refrigerator and discarded 24 hours after preparation.
      • Infants, one litre over 8 to 24 hours, according to age.
      • Adults, drink freely as required, or as directed by the physician. Use only in recommendation dilution.
  • ORS B Plus and ORS Plus
    • Each sachet contains sodium chloride 650 mg, potassium chloride 375 mg, trisodium citrate 725 mg and glucose anhydrous 3.375 g. Ionic concentration (mmol/litre): Na+ 75, K+ 20, Cl- 65, glucose 75 and citrate 10.
    • Dissolve contents of one sachet in 250 ml of cool, boiled water. To be taken orally.
  • UphaLyte
    • Each sachet contains sodium chloride 525 mg, sodium bicarbonate 425 mg, potassium chloride 375 mg and glucose anhydrous 6.25 g. Ionic concentration in mmol/liter (1 sachet in 250 ml water): Na+ 56, K+ 20, Cl- 56, HCO3- 20 and glucose 139.
    • For replacement of water and electrolyte loss associated with diarrhea and vomiting
      • Add 250 ml of boiled, cooled water to the contents of 1 sachet and stir or shake well for 2 to 3 minutes to dissolve.
      • If nausea or vomiting are present, and in infants and young children, drink the solution slowly in sips at shorter intervals.

drugs.notes:
Martindale The Complete Drug Reference, 2020

  • o-Phthaldialdehyde is a bactericidal disinfectant with similar actions to those of glutaral but it is reported to be more active against mycobacteria and to be stable at a wider pH range of 3 to 9. Unlike glutaral it requires no activation before use.
  • A 0.55% aqueous solution of o-phthaldialdehyde is used for high-level disinfection of medical equipment that cannot be sterilised by heat. It is non-corrosive towards most materials. drugs.adverseReactions: Nausea, vomiting, headache, abdominal pain, bronchitis, insomnia and vertigo. drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to oseltamivir phosphate or to any components of the product.
drugs.interactions: No clinically significant interactions known.

  • Premature <38 weeks, 1 mg/kg, >38 weeks-8 months, 3 mg/kg, ≥9 months, 3.5 mg/kg (max 75 mg) 12 H for 5 days oral. Prophylaxis: same dose, daily.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Treatment of influenza
    • The earlier treatment starts, the shorter and less severe the illness. Start within 48 hours (ideally within 24 hours) after onset of symptoms (however, in severe illness, later treatment, e.g. within 4 days of onset, is still of benefit).
    • Adult, child >40 kg, 75 mg twice daily for 5 days.
      • CrCl 30-60 ml/minute, 30 mg twice daily for 5 days.
      • CrCl 10-30 ml/minute, 30 mg once daily for 5 days.
    • Child >1 year
      • <15 kg, 30 mg twice daily for 5 days.
      • 15-23 kg, 45 mg twice daily for 5 days.
      • 23-40 kg, 60 mg twice daily for 5 days.
    • Birth (at term) - 1 year, 3 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days.
  • Prevention of influenza
    • Begin treatment within 2 days of exposure (close contact with an infected person).
    • Adult, child >40 kg, 75 mg once daily for 10 days (has been taken daily for 6 weeks in community outbreaks).
      • CrCl 30-60 ml/minute, 30 mg once daily for 10 days.
      • CrCl 10-30 ml/minute, 30 mg on alternate days for 10 days.
    • Child >1 year
      • <15 kg, 30 mg once daily for 10 days.
      • 15–23 kg, 45 mg once daily for 10 days.
      • 23-40 kg, 60 mg once daily for 10 days.
    • Birth (at term) - 1 year, 3 mg/kg once daily for 10 days.
  • Treatment: this medicine is intended to shorten the time you have symptoms, such as fever, headache, sore muscles, cough and sore throat.
  • Prevention: you may get flu even if you are taking this medicine.
  • Nausea and vomiting in the first couple of days is common with this medicine; take it with food to help reduce this. If swallowing capsules is difficult, you can take the contents of the capsule mixed in soft food, e.g. yoghurt, honey.
  • Neuropsychiatric symptoms including abnormal behaviour, hallucinations and delirium have rarely been described (mainly in children and with oseltamivir use). Influenza can also cause neuropsychiatric symptoms; evidence for oseltamivir is conflicting and the link with peramivir and zanamivir is unclear.

drugs.prescribingRestrictions:
Indication 1: Second-line therapy, in patients who progressed from first-line EGFR TKI therapy. To be prescribed by oncologists and oncology-trained respiratory physicians.
Indication 2: To be prescribed by Oncologist and Consultant Respiratory Physician only.
drugs.dosages: 80 mg once a day until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, taken with or without food at the same time each day. If dose reduction is necessary, then the dose should be reduced to 40 mg taken once daily.
drugs.adverseReactions: Interstitial lung disease; Diarrhea; Decreased appetite; Stevens-Johnson Syndrome; Stomatitis; Rash; Dry skin; Paronychia; Pruritus; QTc interval prolongation; Platelet count decreased; Leucocytes decreased; Lymphocytes decreased; Neutrophils decreased.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients of this product; Concomitant use of St. John’s Wort.
drugs.interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. phenytoin, rifampicin and carbamazepine), Moderate CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. bosentan, efavirenz, etravirine, modafinil); BCRP substrates (e.g. rosuvastatin) and P-gp substrate (e.g. digoxin, dabigatran, aliskiren)
drugs.precautions: EGFR T790M mutation status should be determined. Severe, life-threatening or fatal Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) or ILD-like adverse reactions (e.g. pneumonitis); Stevens-Johnson syndrome; QTc interval prolongation; Changes in cardiac contractility; Keratitis; Elderly patients (>65 years); Low body weight (<50kg); Pregnancy; Breast-feeding
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Swallow whole; do not chew or crush. Alternatively, if you cannot swallow the tablet, put the tablet in one quarter of a cup of plain water, stir until it disperses, then drink it straight away; rinse cup and drink this too.
  • Tell your doctor if you develop new or worsening shortness of breath.
  • This medicine may cause you to bruise and bleed more easily; tell your doctor if this occurs.
  • Interstitial lung disease usually presents as acute onset of dyspnea with cough and fever, with a median time to onset of about 3 months. Pneumonitis has been reported. Stopping Osimertinib usually results in improvement or resolution of symptoms.
  • Monitor ECG and electrolytes periodically in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval.

British National Formulary, 91, 2026

  • Manufacturer advises if a dose is more than 12 hours late, the missed dose should not be taken and the next dose should be taken at the normal time.
  • Manufacturer advises use of effective, non-hormonal, contraception during and for 2 months after treatment in women, and 4 months after treatment in men.

drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • This medicine may increase your chances of getting an infection. Contact your doctor immediately if you develop a fever (temperature of 38°C or more) or any other signs of infection.
  • It may also cause you to bruise and bleed more easily. Tell your doctor if unusual bruising or bleeding occur.
  • During the infusion and for about 2 days afterwards, avoid cold foods or drinks and keep yourself warm because some side effects may occur after exposure to cold temperatures. Some patients may develop the sensation of difficulty breathing or swallowing. Although it can be frightening, this sensation usually goes away quickly.
  • Tell your doctor if you develop fever, difficulty in breathing, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea or if you get pins and needles or numbness of fingers and toes.
  • Do not prepare or administer with equipment containing aluminium as it causes precipitation and loss of potency.

British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • If unexplained respiratory symptoms occur, oxaliplatin should be discontinued until investigations exclude interstitial lung disease and pulmonary fibrosis.
  • Effective contraception required during and for 4 months after treatment in women and 6 months after treatment in men.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Oxcarbazepine (structurally related to carbamazepine) is effective as monotherapy or adjunctive treatment in focal (partial) seizures or generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Unlike carbamazepine, it does not autoinduce its metabolism, and it has less interaction potential. It may be an alternative in patients unable to tolerate carbamazepine.
  • Focal (partial) and generalized tonic-clonic seizures (adjunctive treatment or monotherapy)
    • Adult, initially 300 mg twice daily; then increase daily dose by 600 mg each week, according to response. Usual range, 0.6-2.4 g daily in 2 doses.
    • CrCl <30 ml/minute, initially 300 mg daily; increase slowly according to response.
    • Child >1 month, initially 8-10 mg/kg daily in 2 doses; then increase daily dose by 10 mg/kg each week, according to response. Maximum dose, 60 mg/kg daily in 2 doses.
  • This medicine may cause drowsiness, dizziness or blurred vision especially at the start of treatment or when the dose is increased; if affected, do not drive or operate machinery.
  • Oxcarbazepine may also increase the effects of alcohol.
  • This medicine interacts with many other drugs; ask your doctor or pharmacist before using any other medicine including herbal and over-the-counter products.
  • Tell your doctor immediately if rash, sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, bruising or bleeding occur.
  • Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly unless your doctor tells you to.
  • As there is a high risk of cross-sensitivity, avoid use in patients with a history of hypersensitivity syndrome from carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, oxcarbazepine or eslicarbazepine (the active metabolite of oxcarbazepine). HLA-B*1502 allele significantly increases risk of severe skin reactions. Consider testing for this allele before starting oxcarbazepine in at-risk people, e.g. Asian ancestry (especially Han Chinese, Thai, Malay); if test is positive, avoid use if possible. Allergy or rash with other antiepileptics increases risk of rash with oxcarbazepine.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Elderly people may be more sensitive to anticholinergic adverse effects such as urinary retention, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation and confusion. Adverse effects are usually dose related; start with low dosage and increase cautiously to the lowest effective dose.

drugs.indications:
As a second-line drug in the management of responsive, moderate to severe pain in patients who
i. have difficulty swallowing or
ii. require a low dose oxycodone (<5 mg).
drugs.prescribingRestrictions: To be prescribed by palliative medicine physicians, oncologist, anesthesiologist, hematologist and pain specialists only.
drugs.dosages: Initial dose for opioid naïve patients or patients presenting with severe pain uncontrolled by weaker opioids is 5 mg, 4-6 hourly. The dose should then be carefully titrated, as frequently as once a day if necessary, to achieve pain relief. Maximum daily dose is 400 mg daily. Dosing is individualized and according to product insert/protocol. Should not be used in patients under 18 years.
drugs.adverseReactions: Nausea, constipation, vomiting, respiratory depression, headache, pruritus, insomnia, dizziness, asthenia, somnolence, abdominal pain, chills and fever, hypotension, anorexia, diarrhea, dyspepsia, dysphagia, anxiety, nervousness, tremor, vasodilation, cough, dyspnea, rash.
drugs.contraindications: Respiratory depression, known or suspected paralytic ileus, acute abdomen, delayed gastric emptying, COPD, cor pulmonale, acute or chronic bronchial asthma, hypercarbia, chronic constipation. Concurrent admin of MAOIs or within 2 weeks of discontinuation of use. Moderate to severe hepatic and severe renal impairment. Lactation.
drugs.interactions: Potentiates the effects of tranquilizers, anesthetic, hypnotics, anti-depressants, sedatives, phenothiazines, neuroleptic drugs, other opioids, muscle relaxants and antihypertensives. Concurrent admin of quinidine, a CYP2D6 inhibitor may cause an increase in serum levels and elimination half-life of oxycodone. Cimetidine and CYP3A inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, erythromycin) may inhibit the metabolism of oxycodone.
drugs.precautions: Patient with raised intracranial pressure, hypotension, hypovolemia, toxic psychosis, biliary tract diseases, pancreatitis, inflammatory bowel disorders, prostatic hypertrophy, adrenocortical insufficiency, history of drug abuse or acute alcoholism, delirium tremens, thyroid dysfunction. Mild to moderate renal and mild hepatic impairment. Pregnancy. NPRA Safety Alert (22 Jan 2026): Risk of Oesophageal Dysfunction.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Oxycodone may be tried as an alternative opioid for patients intolerant of morphine.
  • Do not use controlled release tablets for acute pain as slow onset and offset make rapid, safe titration impossible.
  • Naloxone (an opioid antagonist) is intended to reduce opioid-induced GI adverse effects such as constipation. Consider use if optimised regular laxatives for opioid-induced constipation are inadequate; comparative studies with laxatives are lacking.
  • Do not break, crush or chew controlled release tablets.
  • OxyContin® tablets: swallow whole. After putting the tablet in your mouth, make sure you wash it down immediately with an adequate amount of water. If you have problems swallowing the tablets, contact your doctor for a review.
  • This medication may make you feel drowsy and may increase the effects of alcohol. If you are affected, do not drive or operate machinery.
  • If you are very sleepy or have trouble staying awake, stop taking the medication and tell your doctor immediately.
  • Be careful when you stand up as this medicine might make you feel dizzy if you stand up too quickly.
  • Chronic use: look after your teeth and mouth, and get dental checks regularly, as opioids may make your mouth dry which increases risk of dental caries.
  • Constipation: Attention to fluid intake, diet and mobility is required; regular laxative use (e.g. stimulant laxative and stool softener) is essential as soon as chronic opioid treatment is started.

British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • 2 mg oral oxycodone is approximately equivalent to 1 mg parenteral oxycodone.

drugs.indications: For the treatment of moderate to severe pain in patients with cancer and post-operative pain. For the treatment of severe pain requiring the use of a strong opioid.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions: Consultant/specialists for specific indications only, including Geriatricians
drugs.dosages:
Adults over 18 years, the following starting doses are recommended. A gradual increase in dose may be required if analgesia is inadequate or if pain severity increases.
IV Bolus: Dilute to 1 mg/ml in 0.9% saline, 5% dextrose or water for injections. Administer a bolus dose of 1 to 10 mg slowly over 1-2 minutes. Doses should not be administered more frequently than every 4 hours.
IV Infusion: Dilute to 1 mg/ml in 0.9% saline, 5% dextrose or water for injections. A starting dose of 2 mg/hour is recommended. IV PCA: Dilute to 1 mg/ml in 0.9% saline, 5% dextrose or water for injections. Bolus doses of 0.03 mg/kg should be administered with a minimum lock-out time of 5 minutes.
SC Bolus: Use as 10 mg/ml concentration. A starting dose of 5 mg is recommended, repeated at 4-hourly intervals as required. SC Infusion: Dilute in 0.9% saline, 5% dextrose or water for injections if required. A starting dose of 7.5 mg/day is recommended in opioid naive patients, titrating gradually according to symptom control. Cancer patients transferring from oral oxycodone may require much higher doses.

Transferring patients between oral and parenteral oxycodone: The dose should be based on the following ratio: 2 mg of oral oxycodone is equivalent to 1 mg of parenteral oxycodone. It must be emphasized that this is a guide to the dose required. Inter-patient variability requires that each patient is carefully titrated to the appropriate dose.

  • Oxycodone may be tried as an alternative opioid for patients intolerant of morphine.
  • Do not use controlled release tablets for acute pain as slow onset and offset make rapid, safe titration impossible.
  • Naloxone (an opioid antagonist) is intended to reduce opioid-induced GI adverse effects such as constipation. Consider use if optimised regular laxatives for opioid-induced constipation are inadequate; comparative studies with laxatives are lacking.
  • Do not break, crush or chew controlled release tablets.
  • OxyContin® tablets: swallow whole. After putting the tablet in your mouth, make sure you wash it down immediately with an adequate amount of water. If you have problems swallowing the tablets, contact your doctor for a review.
  • This medication may make you feel drowsy and may increase the effects of alcohol. If you are affected, do not drive or operate machinery.
  • If you are very sleepy or have trouble staying awake, stop taking the medication and tell your doctor immediately.
  • Be careful when you stand up as this medicine might make you feel dizzy if you stand up too quickly.
  • Chronic use: look after your teeth and mouth, and get dental checks regularly, as opioids may make your mouth dry which increases risk of dental caries.
  • Constipation: Attention to fluid intake, diet and mobility is required; regular laxative use (e.g. stimulant laxative and stool softener) is essential as soon as chronic opioid treatment is started.

drugs.indications: The management of moderate to severe chronic pain unresponsive to non-narcotic analgesics. The opioid antagonist naloxone in the fixed combination is added to counteract and/or prevent opioid-induced constipation.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions: Consultant/specialists for specific indications only, including Geriatricians.
drugs.dosages: Adults and pediatric patients from 18 years of age, the usual starting dose for opioid-naive patients or patients presenting with moderate to severe chronic pain uncontrolled by weaker opioids is one tablet 10 mg/5 mg at 12 hourly intervals, or one tablet 5 mg/2.5 mg 12-hourly for patients with mild hepatic impairment and patients with renal impairment. The dose should then be cautiously titrated, as frequently as every 1-2 days if necessary, to achieve pain relief.
drugs.adverseReactions: Vertigo, abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, dry mouth, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, asthenic conditions, chills, increased hepatic enzymes, anorexia, muscle spasms, muscle twitching, myalgia, dizziness, headache, somnolence, insomnia, hyperhidrosis, pruritus, rash, decrease in BP & hot flush. For oxycodone HCl: resp depression, miosis, bronchial spasm & spasms of non-striated muscles, cough reflex suppression, gastritis, hiccup, drug withdrawal symptom, fever, faintness, agitation, mood changes, ureteric spasm, urinary abnormalities, urinary tract infection (UTI), bronchospasm, pharyngitis, voice alteration & orthostatic hypotension.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; moderate to severe hepatic impairment; severe resp depression with hypoxia; elevated carbon dioxide levels in the blood; cor pulmonale; cardiac arrhythmias; uncontrolled bronchial asthma; severe COPD; non-opioid-induced paralytic ileus; severe central nervous system (CNS) depression; increased cerebrospinal or intracranial pressure; brain tumor or head injury; uncontrolled convulsive disorders; suspected surgical abdomen; delayed gastric emptying; alcoholism; delirium tremens; concurrent administration of MAOIs & for 2 weeks after cessation. Pregnancy & lactation.
drugs.interactions: Alcohol, Anticholinergic agents, antihypertensive agents, CNS depressants, coumarin derivatives, CYP2D6 & CYP3A4 inhibitors & inducers, metoclopramide, MAOIs, neuromuscular blocking agents, opioid agonist analgesics, opioid agonist-antagonist analgesics.
drugs.precautions:
Geriatric patients: Caution and proper monitoring is warranted. Opioid related adverse effects may be more prominent in this population therefore should be monitored regularly and addressed if occurred.

Must be swallowed whole and must not be broken, chewed or crushed, as this can lead to the rapid release of the active ingredients and absorption of a potentially fatal dose of oxycodone. Mild hepatic impairment, renal impairment, severely impaired pulmonary function, opioid-dependent, substantially decreased resp reserve or pre-existing resp depression, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), hypothyroidism, hypotension, hypertension, hypovolemia, diseases of the biliary tract (e.g. cholelithiasis), pancreatitis, inflammatory bowel disorders, prostatic hypertrophy, adrenocortical insufficiency (Addison's disease), toxic psychosis, myxedema, opioid-induced paralytic ileus, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, epileptic disorders or predisposition to convulsions, pre-op use or within the 1st 12-24 hr post-op, peritoneal carcinomatosis, sub-occlusive syndrome in advanced stages of digestive & pelvic cancers, galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Long-term administration of higher opioid doses. Abrupt cessation of therapy. History of alcohol & drug abuse. May affect the ability to drive & operate machinery. Pregnancy & lactation. Children or adolescents.

drugs.indications:
i) Management of moderate to severe chronic cancer pain non-responsive to morphine in accordance with WHO step-wise ladder of chronic pain management.
ii) As a second line treatment of chronic non-cancer pain when treatments with adjuvant analgesics and non-pharmacological approach failed.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions: Indication (ii): Initiated by Pain, Palliative Specialists or Geriatricians only
drugs.dosages: Adults, elderly and children over 12 years, usual starting dose for opioid-naive patients or patients presenting with moderate to severe pain uncontrolled by weaker opioids (especially if they are receiving concurrent sedatives, muscle relaxants or other CNS medicines) is 10 mg 12 hourly. The dose should then be carefully titrated with longitudinal patient monitoring, assessing whether the pain is opioid responsive and providing the patient significant pain relief. Patients with renal or hepatic impairment: The recommended adult starting dose should be reduced by 1/3 to 1/2, and each patient should be titrated to adequate pain control according to their clinical situation.
drugs.adverseReactions: Bradycardia, chest pain, palpitations, ST depression, supraventricular tachycardia, tinnitus, vertigo, miosis, visual impairment, nausea, vomiting, constipation, asthenia, fatigue, chills, fever, hepatobiliary disorders, immune system disorders, decreased appetite, dizziness, headache and somnolence, bronchospasm, dyspnea, pharyngitis, voice alteration, pruritus.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to opioids, acute respiratory depression, cor pulmonale, cardiac arrhythmias, acute asthma or other obstructive airways disease, paralytic ileus, suspected surgical abdomen, severe renal impairment, delayed gastric emptying, acute alcoholism, brain tumor, increased cerebrospinal or intracranial pressure, head injury, severe CNS depression, convulsive disorders, delirium tremens, hypercarbia. Concurrent MAOIs (or within 2 weeks of discontinuation). Pre-operative or within 24 hours post-operative. Lactation.
drugs.interactions: Anticholinergics, antihypertensives, CNS depressants including sedatives or hypnotics, general anesthetics, phenothiazines, other tranquillizers, alcohol, other opioids & neuroleptics; muscle relaxants, coumarin derivatives, metoclopramide, MAOIs, neuromuscular blockers, opioid analgesics, drugs that involve cytochrome P450 enzyme system e.g. CYP3A4, CYP2D6.
drugs.precautions:
Geriatric patients: Caution and proper monitoring is warranted. Opioid related adverse effects may be more prominent in this population therefore should be monitored regularly and addressed if occurred.

Use with caution in opioid-dependent patients and in patients with hypotension, hypovolemia, diseases of the biliary tract, pancreatic, inflammatory bowel disorders, prostatic hypertrophy, adrenocortical insufficiency, toxic psychosis, chronic pulmonary, renal or hepatic disease, myxedema and debilitated elderly of infirm patients. Patients who undergo cordotomy or other pain-relieving surgical procedures should not receive Oxycontin tablets for 24 hours before surgery.

drugs.dosages:
Newborn up to 4 weeks, 1 drop. Infant 1-12 month, 1-2 drop.

Doses to be given twice or three times daily
drugs.adverseReactions: Burning or dryness of nasal mucosa, sneezing, blocked nose (reactive hyperemia), palpitations, hypertension, insomnia, headache
drugs.contraindications: Rhinitis sicca; Hypersensitivity to active ingredient or one of other ingredients
drugs.interactions: Overdosage or swallowing of 0.01% oxymetazoline nasal drops and use of tricyclic antidepressants or MAOIs simultaneously or immediately prior to administration of oxymetazoline can lead to an increase in blood pressure

drugs.notes:
Product leaflet, accessed 2022 - Oxy-nase

  • For relief of nasal congestion
    • Oxy-nase Nasal Spray (0.05%): For adults & children 6 years of age and older, 2 to 3 sprays into each nostril twice daily, morning and evening.
    • Oxy-nase Paediatric Nasal Spray (0.025%): For children 2 to 6 years of age, administer 2 to 3 sprays in each nostril twice daily, morning and evening.
  • Do not exceed the recommended dosage and do not use for longer than 3 days.

Product leaflet, accessed 2022 - Iliadin

  • Iliadin Baby Up to 1 Year Nasal Drops (0.01%)
    • Newborn up to 4 weeks, instill 1 drop into each nostril BD-TDS.
    • 5th week up to 1 year, instill 1-2 drops into each nostril BD-TDS.
  • Iliadin Child 1-6 Years Nasal Drops (0.025%)
    • Children 1-6 years, instill 1-2 drops BD-TDS.
  • Iliadin Adult and Children 6+ Nasal Drops (0.05%)
    • Adult & children ≥6 years, instill 1-2 drops into each nostril BD-TDS.
  • Iliadin Adults Nasal Spray (0.05%)
    • Adult & children ≥6 years, spray 1 puff into each nostril BD-TDS.
  • Not to be used for >10 consecutive days. Long-term use & high doses may result to rebound effect and drug-induced rhinitis.
    • A treatment-free period of several days should precede any repeated use.
  • After opening the pack, the Iliadin decongestant nasal drop/spray should not be used longer than 6 months.

Product leaflet, accessed 2023 - ClariClear

  • Symptomatic relief of nasal and nasal pharyngeal congestion due to the common cold, sinusitis, hay fever or other upper respiratory allergies
    • Adults and children 6 years of age and older, 2 or 3 sprays into each nostril twice daily, morning and evening.
  • With the head upright, place the sprays nozzle into the nostril without completely occluding the nostril. During each administration, the patient should bend his head slightly forward and spray the dose into each nostril by squeezing the bottle rapidly and strongly.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Do not use intranasal decongestants for the common cold in children <6 years of age.
  • Encourage use of sodium chloride 0.9% solution (nose drops, irrigation or spray) in preference to an intranasal sympathomimetic, especially for children.
  • If nasal congestion impairs feeding in infants, use sodium chloride 0.9% nose drops (a few drops in each nostril just before feed) to loosen and liquefy mucus secretions.
  • Keep dose and length of treatment (up to 5 days) to a minimum to reduce risk of rebound congestion (may take several weeks to reverse).
  • Maximal effect of oxymetazoline, tramazoline and xylometazoline lasts for 6 hours. Maximal effect of phenylephrine lasts for 4 hours.
  • Ephedrine is still used in extemporaneous preparations. It is less likely to cause rebound symptoms than more potent agents, e.g. oxymetazoline, phenylephrine.

British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • Symptoms of nasal congestion associated with allergic rhinitis, the common cold and sinusitis may be relieved by the short-term use (usually not longer than 7 days) of decongestant nasal drops and sprays. These all contain sympathomimetic drugs which exert their effect by vasoconstriction of the mucosal blood vessels which in turn reduces edema of the nasal mucosa.
  • Their use, especially with longer durations, can give rise to rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa) on withdrawal, due to a secondary vasodilatation with a subsequent temporary increase in nasal congestion. This in turn tempts the further use of the decongestant, leading to a vicious cycle of events; tolerance with reduced effect may also be seen with excessive use.

drugs.indications:
i) Induction of labor
ii) Inadequate uterine effort
iii) Management of third stage of labor
iv) Prevention and treatment of post-partum hemorrhage
v) As adjunctive therapy for the management of incomplete, inevitable or missed abortion
drugs.dosages:
i & ii) Initiate at 2 milliunits/min, may be increased by 4 milliunits/min gradually at 30 minute intervals. Dose may be decreased once a contraction pattern similar to normal labor is achieved and labor has progressed to 5-6 cm dilation. Maximum dose of oxytocin for multiparae-16 milliunits/min and nulliparae-32 milliunits/min.
iii) IV/IM: 5-10 units.
iv) IV: 5-10 units followed by IV infusion at 10 units/hour.
v) Initial: 5 units given via slow inj over 5 minutes, may be followed by an infusion at a rate of 20-40 milliunits/minute as necessary.

The dosing is individualized based on maternal, fetal response and product insert/protocol.
drugs.adverseReactions: Gastrointestinal upsets, water intoxication resulting from large amounts of solution or too rapid infusion, cardiac arrhythmias
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to oxytocin, significant cephalopelvic disproportion, unfavorable fetal positions, fetal distress, hypertonic or hyperactive uterus, contraindicated vaginal delivery
drugs.interactions: Prostaglandins, inhalation anesthetics, vasoconstrictor agents
drugs.precautions: For induction or enhancement only as IV infusion, careful monitoring of fetal heart rate and uterine contractions are required
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Oxytocin has weak antidiuretic properties and may contribute to maternal and neonatal hyponatraemia if used in high doses with large volumes of fluid. Pulmonary oedema without hyponatraemia may also occur.
  • When using an infusion, monitor fluid balance to prevent water intoxication.
  • It is unclear whether induction or augmentation of labour using uterine stimulants increases the risk of amniotic fluid embolism
  • In the active management of third stage of labour, oxytocin is generally preferred to the combination of ergometrine with oxytocin (Syntometrine®) which:
    • is associated with a higher incidence of nausea, vomiting and hypertension
    • has little advantage over oxytocin alone in terms of blood loss (small reduction in risk of blood loss >500 ml; no difference in risk of blood loss >1000 ml)

i) 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hours every 3 weeks.
ii) First-line: 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hour followed by a platinum compound every 3 weeks or 135 mg/m2 IV over 24 hours followed by a platinum compound every 3 weeks. Second-line: 175 mg/m2 over 3 hours every 3 weeks.

drugs.adverseReactions: Alopecia, myelosuppression, severe neutropenia, peripheral neuropathy, arrhythmias, hypotension, hypersensitivity reactions, arthralgia, myalgia
drugs.contraindications: History of hypersensitivity reaction to paclitaxel or polyoxyethylated castor oil (Cremophor EL) or any component of preparation. Pregnancy, lactation
drugs.interactions: Doxorubicin, live vaccines, phenytoin, ketoconazole, St John's Wort
drugs.precautions: Severe neutropenia, severe hepatic impairment. Caution in patients with ischemic heart disease, myocardial infarction and conduction defects. Taxane to be given first when used in combination with platinum analogue to avoid myelosuppression. Increased risk of infection by live vaccines
drugs.notes:
Lexicomp, 2021

  • Premedication with dexamethasone (20 mg orally at 12 and 6 hours prior to the dose [reduce dexamethasone dose to 10 mg orally with advanced HIV disease]), diphenhydramine (50 mg IV 30 to 60 minutes prior to the dose), and cimetidine or famotidine (IV 30 to 60 minutes prior to the dose) is recommended.

British National Formulary 81, 2021

  • Paclitaxel is available as both conventional and albumin-bound formulations. The different formulations vary in their licensed indications, pharmacokinetics, dosage and administration, and are not interchangeable.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Myelosuppression is dose-related and limiting. Neutropenia and anemia are common; thrombocytopenia occurs less frequently. Neutrophil nadir generally occurs 10-12 days after a dose with recovery by about day 15-21. Platelet nadir occurs 8-9 days after a dose.
  • Peripheral neuropathy (symptoms include paresthesia, dysesthesia, pain and burning) but motor neuropathy may also occur. Frequency and severity increase with cumulative doses of docetaxel or paclitaxel and are also dose dependent for paclitaxel. Reduce dose or stop taxane treatment if severe.
  • Monitor ECG throughout infusion if previous doses have caused cardiac conduction abnormalities.
  • Conventional product:
    • premedicate with dexamethasone, an antihistamine and an H2antagonist to reduce the incidence and severity of hypersensitivity reactions, see relevant protocol for details.
    • 150 mg of paclitaxel injection contains approximately 10 g of ethanol (the same as a standard drink).
    • Use non-PVC container and giving set. Infuse IV over 1, 3 or 24 hours (according to protocol) via an in-line 0.22 micrometre (micron) filter. Avoid extravasation. May also be given via intraperitoneal infusion (for ovarian cancer).
  • Albumin-bound
    • Albumin-bound has a lower incidence of hypersensitivity reactions, and administration is easier as, unlike the conventional product, it does not contain polyoxyl 35 castor oil and ethanol
    • Does not require premedication to prevent hypersensitivity reactions.
    • PVC containers and giving sets may be used. In-line filtration is not recommended. Infuse IV over 30 minutes. Avoid extravasation.

British National Formulary 85, 2023

  • Breast cancer; Pancreatin adenocarcinoma
    • Adult, by intravenous infusion, access specialist resources for dosing information.
  • Paclitaxel is available as conventional and albumin-bound formulations; these formulations are not interchangeable.

drugs.indications: Indicated for the treatment of hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine based therapy in postmenopausal women.
drugs.dosages: 125 mg capsule taken orally once daily for 21 consecutive days followed by 7 days off treatment to comprise a complete cycle of 28 days. Palbociclib should be taken with food. For dose modification, refer package insert.
drugs.adverseReactions: Infections, neutropenia, leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, decreased appetite, dysgeusia, stomatitis, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, alopecia, rash, dry skin, fatigue, asthenia, pyrexia, interstitial lung disease/non-infectious pneumonitis. NPRA Safety Alert (10 Feb 2026): Risk of Venous Thromboembolism.
drugs.contraindications: None
drugs.interactions: CYP3A inhibitors, CYP3A inducers and sensitive CYP3A substrate with narrow therapeutic index. Refer package insert for details
drugs.precautions: Neutropenia, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, embryo-fetal toxicity, lactation, severe hepatic impairment. NPRA Safety Alert (10 Feb 2026): Risk of Venous Thromboembolism.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Swallow capsule whole; do not chew, crush or open them. Take with food at the same time each day.
  • Avoid grapefruit juice as it may increase the risk of side effects with palbociclib.
  • Myelosuppression includes neutropenia, anemia and thrombocytopenia; it is generally rapidly reversible with dose reduction or interruption.

British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • Manufacturer advises to take palbociclib at the same time each day; if a dose is missed, the missed dose should not be taken and the next dose should be taken at the usual time.
  • Manufacturer advises if concomitant use with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce palbociclib dose to 75 mg once daily. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is stopped, increase the palbociclib dose (after 3-5 half lives of the inhibitor) to the dose used before the CYP3A4 inhibitor.
  • Manufacturer advises monitor full blood count prior to starting therapy, at the start of each cycle, on day 14 of the first 2 cycles and as clinically indicated.
  • Manufacturer advises effective contraception in women of childbearing potential during treatment for at least 3 weeks after completing treatment. Male patients should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 14 weeks after completing treatment if their partner is of childbearing potential.
  • Interstitial lung disease and pneumonitis, in some cases severe or fatal, have been reported in patients being treated with CDK4/6 inhibitors, such as palbociclib. Patients should be advised to seek advice right away if symptoms indicative of interstitial lung disease and pneumonitis, such as cough or dyspnea, occur.

drugs.indications: Second or third line treatment of acute and maintenance treatment of schizophrenia in adults
drugs.dosages: Initiation, deltoid IM 150 mg eq on Day1, followed by deltoid IM 100 mg eq on one week later. Maintenance, monthly dose of 75 mg eq (this can be increased or decreased based on individual patient's tolerability and/or efficacy). These monthly maintenance dose can be administered in either the deltoid or gluteal muscle
drugs.adverseReactions: Insomnia, headache, agitation, somnolence, sedation, dizziness, injection site pain, akathisia, extrapyramidal disorder, constipation, nausea, vomiting, nasopharyngitis, bradycardia, bundle branch block, postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, tachycardia, blood cholesterol increased, blood glucose increased, convulsion, dizziness postural, drooling, dysarthria, dyskinesia, dystonia, hypertonia, lethargy, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, oromandibular dystonia, parkinsonism, psychomotor hyperactivity, syncope, oculogyric crisis, eye rolling, vision blurred, amenorrhea, erectile dysfunction, galactorrhea, gynecomastia, menstruation irregular, sexual dysfunction
drugs.contraindications: Moderate to severe renal impairment, dementia-related psychosis, lactation
drugs.interactions: Centrally acting drugs, alcohol, levodopa & other dopamine agonists, carbamazepine. Drugs known to prolong QT interval
drugs.precautions: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome, congenital long QT syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, hyperglycemia & diabetes mellitus, hyperprolactinemia, cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease or conditions predisposing to hypotension. Monitor complete blood count regularly. History of seizures & cardiac arrhythmias, risk for aspiration pneumonia. Conditions that contribute to core body temperature elevation or dehydration. Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies. Pregnancy. Elderly. Adolescents & children. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. NPRA Safety Alert (17 June 2014): Risk of intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) during and after cataract surgery.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Paliperidone is the major active metabolite of risperidone.
  • Although the once-monthly long-acting injection is indicated for acute schizophrenia, it may be more suitable for those with mild-to-moderate symptoms, particularly if they have responded to oral paliperidone or risperidone in the past.

drugs.genericName: Paliperidone 175 mg/0.875 ml Prolonged-Release for Intramuscular Injection
drugs.indications: For the maintenance treatment of schizophrenia in adult patients who have been adequately treated with the 1-month paliperidone palmitate injectable product for at least four months.
drugs.dosages: Apply 3.5 as a dose multiplier to the previous 1-month injection dose, and administer every 3 months
drugs.adverseReactions: Parkinsonism, sedation/somnolence, tremor, tachycardia, nausea, transaminases increased, musculoskeletal pain, back pain, amenorrhea, menstrual disorder.
drugs.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paliperidone, risperidone, or to any of the components in the formulation. Breast-feeding women. History of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome with the use of any paliperidone product. History of clinically significant QT prolongation with the use of any paliperidone product. History of clinically significant drug-induced leukopenia/neutropenia with the use of any paliperidone product.
drugs.interactions: Drugs known to prolong the QT interval, psychostimulants, centrally acting drugs, drugs inducing orthostatic hypotension, other antipsychotics, alcohol
drugs.precautions: Use in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment, severe hepatic impairment, <18 years of age, elderly, and pregnant women. History of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome with the use of other drugs. Development of tardive dyskinesia and extrapyramidal symptoms (including those on concomitant psychostimulants and paliperidone). Prolongation of QT interval. Patients with known cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, or conditions that predispose the patient to hypotension. History of seizures or other conditions that potentially lower the seizure threshold. Patients at risk of aspiration pneumonia. History of a clinically significant low white blood cell count or a drug-induced leukopenia/neutropenia. Performing activities requiring mental alertness. Inadvertent injection into a blood vessel. Patients with Parkinson's disease of Dementia with Lewy Bodies.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Paliperidone is the major active metabolite of risperidone.

drugs.dosages: Initially 1-2 capsules with each meal. May increase to 5-15 capsules daily. Dosing is individualized and according to product insert/protocol

drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Pancreatic enzymes are essential for fat, carbohydrate and protein digestion. Supplements aim to correct enzymatic deficiency. All products are of porcine origin.
  • Dose must be individualised and is guided by stool quality and quantity, and nutritional status. Titrate to the lowest effective dose. Specialist and dietitian supervision is recommended.
  • Maximum dose:
    • >18 years, 80000 units of lipase per meal.
    • <18 years, 10000 units of lipase/kg daily.
  • Take this medicine with meals and snacks.
    • Granules: add the granules to a small amount of acidic soft food or juice (e.g. apple sauce or juice) and swallow immediately with water. Avoid mixing with hot liquid or food as heat can destroy it. Do not crush or chew the granules.
    • Capsules: Swallow capsules whole with a glass of water or open them and add the granules to a small amount of acidic soft food or juice (e.g. apple sauce or juice) then proceed as above. Do not crush or chew the capsule.

  • Pancreatin is inactivated by gastric acid therefore manufacturer advises pancreatin preparations are best taken with food (or immediately before or after food).
  • Since pancreatin is inactivated by heat, excessive heat should be avoided if preparations are mixed with liquids or food; manufacturer advises the resulting mixtures should not be kept for more than one hour and any left-over food or liquid containing pancreatin should be discarded.
  • Enteric-coated preparations deliver a higher enzyme concentration in the duodenum (provided the capsule contents are swallowed whole without chewing).
  • Manufacturer advises gastro-resistant granules should be mixed with slightly acidic soft food or liquid such as apple juice, and then swallowed immediately without chewing. Capsules containing enteric-coated granules can be opened and the granules administered in the same way.

drugs.notes:

  • Moderate-to-severe pain
    • Adult, 1-2 tablets every 4-6 hours if needed, up to a maximum of 8 tablets daily.

    • People with normal codeine metabolism metabolize 30 mg of codeine to approximately 3 mg of morphine
    • Some people are unlikely to obtain pain relief with codeine due to a genetic lack of CYP2D6, e.g. 6-10% of Caucasians and 1-2% of Asians
    • Some people are ultra-rapid metabolizers and may achieve higher morphine concentrations, increasing their risk of toxicity (those affected include up to 10% of Caucasians, 1-2% of Asians, 21% of people from the Middle East, e.g. Saudi Arabians, and 29% of Ethiopians)
  • Beware of potential for over-use, leading to codeine dependence and increased risk of paracetamol toxicity.

Pharmaceutical Compounding and Dispensing, 2010

  • Both Yellow and White Soft Paraffin BP are widely used ointment bases. They are both semi-solid mixtures of hydrocarbons obtained from petroleum.
  • White Soft Paraffin BP has been highly refined and is decolourised (bleached Yellow Soft Paraffin BP). Both have similar properties with a melting point range of 38-56°C (the melting point range is because the melting point may vary slightly from batch to batch).
  • Traditionally Yellow Soft Paraffin BP has been used when an ointment includes dark-coloured ingredients (e.g. Coal Tar BP or Ichthammol BP). White Soft Paraffin BP was reserved for products with colourless, white or pale ingredients.
  • It is accepted nowadays that although White Soft Paraffin BP may produce products that are more 'pleasing to the eye', the unbleached form, Yellow Soft Paraffin BP, is less likely to cause sensitivity reactions in susceptible patients.

Hepatic impairment, pharmacokinetics of pegfilgrastim is not expected to be affected by hepatic impairment. drugs.adverseReactions: Bone pain, arthralgia, myalgia, back, limb, musculo-skeletal and neck pain; injection site pain and erythema, chest pain (non-cardiac), headache, nausea; elevations in uric acid, alkaline phosphatase and lactate dehydrogenase; rare cases of splenic rupture, Sweet's syndrome, cutaneous vasculitis; hypersensitivity-type reactions including skin rash, urticaria, angioedema, dyspnea, erythema, flushing, hypotension, anaphylaxis, thrombocytopenia, aortitis.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to pegfilgrastim, filgrastim, E. coli derived proteins, or to any excipients
drugs.interactions: Pegfilgrastim should not be given at the same time as cytotoxic chemotherapy due to the increased risk of myelosuppression (should be administered approximately 24 hours after cytotoxic chemotherapy).
drugs.precautions: Splenic rupture or enlarged spleen have been reported; patients with left upper abdominal or shoulder tip pain should be evaluated for development of splenomegaly or splenic rupture. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) may occur; monitor patients for pulmonary symptoms. Capillary leak syndrome has been reported which is characterized by hypotension, hypoalbuminemia, edema and hemoconcentration. Caution in patients with existing sickle cell disorders as severe sickle cell crisis may occur. Not approved for myeloid malignancies and myelodysplasia. Monitor platelet count and hematocrit regularly. Not recommended to be used during pregnancy as there are no or limited amount of data. Aortitis has been reported after G-CSF administration in healthy subjects and in cancer patients. The symptoms experienced included fever, abdominal pain, malaise, back pain and increased inflammatory markers (e.g. C-reactive protein and white blood cell count). In most cases aortitis was diagnosed by CT scan and generally resolved after withdrawal of G-CSF. NPRA Safety Alert (19 & 27 Aug 2014): Risk of Capillary Leak Syndrome.
drugs.notes:

  • Treatment should be withdrawn in patients who develop signs of pulmonary infiltration.

  • Store in a refrigerator (2-8°C).

drugs.indications:
i) For patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer where the disease relapses within 6 months after completion of the initial platinum-based chemotherapy.
ii) For patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer where the disease responds to first-line platinum-based therapy but relapses 12 months or more after completion of the initial platinum based chemotherapy.
drugs.dosages: 50 mg/m2 IV every 4 weeks for as long as the disease does not progress & patient continues to tolerate treatment. For doses <90 mg: dilute in 250 ml Dextrose 5 % in Water. For doses >90 mg: dilute in 500 ml Dextrose 5 % in Water. To minimize the risk of infusion reactions, the initial dose is administered at a rate no greater than 1 mg/minute. Renal impairment, no dose adjustment required in patients with creatinine clearance 30-156 ml/min, no pharmacokinetic data are available in patients with creatinine clearance of less than 30 ml/min. Hepatic impairment, at initiation of therapy: Bilirubin 1.2-3.0 mg/dl, the first dose is reduced by 25%, Bilirubin >3.0 mg/dl, the first dose is reduced by 50%.
drugs.adverseReactions: Infusion-associated reactions, stomatitis, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, myelosuppression, leukopenia, anemia, neutropenia, peripheral edema, oral moniliasis, mouth ulceration.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity reactions to any of the components of the product or to doxorubicin HCl. Should not be used to treat AIDS-KS that may be effectively treated with local therapy or systemic α-interferon. Pregnancy and Lactation.
drugs.interactions: Caution should be exercised in the concomitant use of drugs known to interact with standard doxorubicin HCl. Other cytotoxic agents especially myelotoxic agents.
drugs.precautions: CV disease, impaired cardiac function; patients who have received other anthracyclines, myelosuppression, diabetic patients.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Tell your doctor or nurse immediately if you feel any pain, stinging or burning during the injection or infusion.
  • Myelosuppression is common, affecting white cells, and to a lesser degree, platelets and red cells. The white cell count nadir occurs about 10 days after a dose, with recovery by about 21 days.
  • Urine may appear red for 1-2 days after dose.
  • Tell your doctor if you develop numbness, tingling, pain, redness, blistering or swelling of your hands or feet.

British National Formulary 81, 2021

  • Higher cumulative doses are associated with cardiomyopathy and it is usual to limit total cumulative doses to 450 mg/m2.
  • Liposomal formulations of doxorubicin may reduce the incidence of cardiotoxicity and lower the potential for local necrosis, but infusion reactions, sometimes severe, may occur. Hand-foot syndrome (painful, macular reddening skin eruptions) occurs commonly with liposomal doxorubicin and may be dose limiting. It can occur after 2-3 treatment cycles and may be prevented by cooling hands and feet and avoiding socks, gloves, or tight-fitting footwear. It may also occur with non-liposomal formulations.
  • Manufacturer advises effective contraception during and for at least 6 months after treatment in men or women.

Lexicomp, 2022

  • Store intact vials at 2-8°C; do not freeze.

  • Irinotecan (liposomal) is associated with a moderate emetic potential. Premedicate with a corticosteroid and an antiemetic 30 minutes prior to infusion.
  • Fatal neutropenic sepsis occurred in 0.8% of patients receiving irinotecan (liposomal). Severe or life-threatening neutropenic fever or sepsis occurred in 3% and severe or life-threatening neutropenia occurred in 20% of patients receiving irinotecan (liposomal) in combination with fluorouracil and leucovorin.
  • Severe diarrhea occurred in 13% of patients receiving irinotecan (liposomal) in combination with fluorouracil and leucovorin. Do not administer irinotecan (liposomal) to patients with bowel obstruction.
  • Store intact vials at 2-8°C; do not freeze. Protect from light.

British National Formulary 83, 2022

  • Irinotecan is available as both conventional and liposomal formulations. These different formulations vary in their licensed indications, pharmacokinetics, dosage and administration, and are not interchangeable.
  • Onivyde has been associated with reports of serious thromboembolic events, such as pulmonary embolism, venous thrombosis and arterial thromboembolism.
