drugs.genericName: Varicella Virus Vaccine Live Attenuated Injection
drugs.indications: Immunization against varicella virus infection.
drugs.dosages: 0.5 ml by SC. Dosing is according to product insert.
drugs.adverseReactions: Fever, rash, urticaria, erythema, pruritus. Rarely, local reaction, anaphylactoid symptoms
drugs.contraindications: Reinforcement therapy for leukemia or extensive therapy using strong immunosuppressives. Acute myelogenous leukemia or malignant lymphoma
drugs.interactions: Transfusion and administration of gamma-globulin preparations: The vaccine may not be effective in those receiving blood or gamma-globulin preparation within 3 month before vaccination. Vaccination of such individuals should be delayed until equal or more than 3 months has elapsed. For those receiving high dose gamma-globulin therapy, i.e. equal or more than 200 mg/kg, e.g. patients with Kawasaki disease or acute immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP), vaccination should be delayed until equal or more than 6 months has elapsed. If gamma-globulin is administered within 14 days after administration of the vaccine, the vaccine may not be effective. Such individuals should be re-vaccinated equal or more than 3 months after the initial vaccination. Other live vaccine preparations: Those receiving other live vaccines, e.g. oral polio, measles, mumps, rubella, BCG or yellow fever vaccine, are advised to wait until equal or more than 4 weeks has elapsed before being vaccinated. Incompatibilities: The vaccine should not be mixed with other vaccines or medications in the same syringe
drugs.precautions: Discontinue maintenance chemotherapy equal or less than 1 week prior to injection and recommence therapy after equal or more than 1 week after injection. Malignant solid tumors, women of child-bearing potential should practice adequate contraceptive measures 1 month prior to vaccination and 2 month after vaccination. Cardiovascular, kidney, liver, hematological or developmental abnormalities. History of seizures, diagnosed immunodeficiency states, abnormal immune system function. Concomitant immunosuppressive therapy. Vaccine may not effective in patients receiving blood or gamma-globulin preparation within 3 month prior to vaccination. Other live viral vaccines should only be given equal or more than 4 weeks after Okavax
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Varicella vaccine and zoster vaccine are not interchangeable (zoster vaccine contains a much higher viral titre)

MIMS, 2022

  • Varilrix
    • The lyophilised vaccine should be stored in a refrigerator (2°C-8°C) and protected from light. The solvent can be stored in the refrigerator or at ambient temperature. The lyophilised vaccine is not affected by freezing.
    • When supplies of Varilrix are distributed from a central cold store, transport must be done under refrigerator conditions especially in hot climates.
    • After reconstitution, it is recommended that the vaccine be injected as soon as possible.
    • It has been demonstrated that the reconstituted vaccine may be kept for up to 90 minutes at room temperature (25°C) and up to 8 hours in the refrigerator (2°C-8°C).
  • Varivax

drugs.genericName: Varicella Zoster Immunoglobulin (Human) 25 IU/ml Solution for Infusion
drugs.notes:
Product leaflet, accessed 2022

  • Varitect CP is used for prophylaxis of varicella infection after exposure for
    • Children with negative history of varicella who are receiving immunosuppressive, cytostatic or radiotherapy or suffer from hereditary immunodeficiencies;
    • Immunocompromised adults who, after careful evaluation are believed susceptible and have significant exposure;
    • Newborns of mothers who develop chicken pox within 5 days before and 2 days after delivery;
    • Premature infants whose mothers have negative histories of varicella, as long as they require hospital care;
    • Premature infants of less than 28 weeks of gestation or with a birth weight of 1000 g or less, regardless of maternal varicella history;
  • As adjuvant therapy of severe or complicated varicella zoster especially in immunocompromised patients.
  • Prevention of chicken pox
    • The usual dose is 1 ml (25 IU) per kg body weight. In repeated exposure, e.g. household contact, higher doses are preferable. For post-exposure prophylaxis, Varitect CP should be administered as soon as possible and not later than 96 hours after exposure.
  • Treatment of zoster infections
    • The usual dose is 1-2 ml (25-50 IU) per kg body weight, with additional applications depending on the course of clinical manifestations.
  • Varitect CP is a solution for intravenous infusion (infusion into a vein). It should be brought to room or body temperature before use. Varitect CP will be infused at an initial infusion rate of 0.1 ml per kg body weight per hour during the first 10 minutes. If well tolerated, the rate of administration may gradually be increased to a maximum of 1.0 ml per kg body weight per hour for the remainder of the infusion.
  • Too much Varitect CP can cause fluid overload and hyper viscosity (over-thickening) of the blood, especially if you are over 65 years of age and/or have impaired renal function.
  • Store in a refrigerator (2-8°C). Do not freeze. Protect from light.

drugs.adverseReactions: Abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, passage of gas, tremor, vertigo, "pounding" in head, bronchial constriction, sweating, urticaria, cutaneous gangrene.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to vasopressin, poor distal limb perfusion, hyperbilirubinemia and acute cardiac or bowel ischemia
drugs.interactions: Carbamazepine, chlorpropamide, clofibrate, urea, fludrocortisone, tricyclic antidepressants, noradrenaline, lithium, heparin and alcohol

drugs.notes:
Lexicomp, 2024

  • Septic shock and other vasodilatory shock states (adjunctive agent)
    • Considered as adjunctive use when goal mean arterial pressure (MAP) not achieved with initial catecholamine vasopressor (eg, norepinephrine) or to decrease catecholamine vasopressor dosage requirements. In general, maintain goal MAP (eg, ~65 mm Hg); consider use if patient is in shock or has hypoperfusion during or after fluid resuscitation.
  • Shock, sepsis
    • Adult, continuous infusion: IV: 0.03 units/minute added to norepinephrine as a fixed dose (not titrated); usual dosage range: 0.01 to 0.04 units/minute; doses >0.04 units/minute should be reserved for salvage therapy due to potential risk of ischemic complications (eg, skin, cardiac, splanchnic).
    • Discontinuation in septic shock: Multiple studies describe clinically significant hypotension when vasopressin is discontinued prior to norepinephrine. When discontinuing therapy, consider slowly tapering by 0.01 units/minute every 30 to 60 minutes to reduce the risk of hypotension; monitor MAP when discontinuing vasopressin.
  • Shock, post-cardiotomy
    • Adult, continuous infusion: IV: Initial: 0.03 units/minute. If the target blood pressure response is not achieved, titrate up by 0.005 units/minute at 10- to 15-minute intervals (maximum dose: 0.1 units/minute). After target blood pressure has been maintained for 8 hours without the use of catecholamines, taper by 0.005 units/minute every hour as tolerated to maintain target blood pressure.
  • Storage
    • Store intact vials between 2°C and 8° Do not freeze.
    • May also remove intact vials from refrigeration and store at 20-25°C for up to 12 months or manufacturer expiration date, whichever is earlier.

JKN Selangor Dilution Protocol, 2017

  • IV infusion
    • Dilute with diluent to a concentration of 0.1-1 IU/ml.
    • Example: 20 IU in 50 ml diluent (0.4 IU/ml).
    • Diluent: NS, D5.

drugs.prescriberCategory: DELISTED FROM MOHMF 2021-3 because no registered product in Malaysia, no usage since 2018 and alternative is available.
drugs.indications: As an adjunct in anesthesia to produce skeletal muscle relaxation
drugs.dosages: Adult & neonates >5 months, initial: 80-100 mcg/kg as inj. Maintenance: 20-30 mcg/kg, adjust according to response. Alternatively, as continuous infusion at 0.8-1.4 mcg/kg/min after initial IV dose of 40-100 mcg/kg. Neonate and infant up to 4 months, initially 10-20 mcg/kg, then incremental dose to achieve response
drugs.adverseReactions: Changes in vital signs, prolonged neuromuscular block e.g., vary from skeletal muscle weakness to profound and prolonged skeletal muscle paralysis resulting in respiratory insufficiency or apnea. Anaphylactic reactions e.g., bronchospasm, cardiovascular changes (e.g. hypotension, tachycardia, circulatory collapse, shock), and cutaneous changes (e.g. angioedema, urticaria). Anaphylactoid reactions e.g. possible occurrence of itching and erythematous reactions at the site of injection.
drugs.contraindications: Known former anaphylactic reactions to vecuronium or bromide ion
drugs.interactions:
Increased Effect: Anesthetics e.g., halothane, ether, enflurane, isoflurane, methoxyflurane, cyclopropane, thiopentone, methohexital, ketamine, fentanyl, γ-hydroxybutyrate, etomidate, propanidid. Other nondepolarizing muscle relaxants, prior administration of suxamethonium, aminoglycoside and polypeptide antibiotics, diuretics, β-adrenergic-blocking agents, thiamine, MAO inhibiting agents, quinidine, protamine, phenytoin, α-adrenergic-blocking agents, imidazole, metronidazole.

Decreased Effect: Neostigmine, edrophonium, pyridostigmine, prior chronic administration of corticosteroids, noradrenaline, azathioprine, theophylline, KCl, NaCl, CaCl2, prior chronical administration of phenytoin or carbamazepine.

Variable Effect: Depolarizing muscle relaxants given after the administration of vecuronium bromide may produce potentiation or attenuation of the neuromuscular-blocking effect.
drugs.precautions: Pregnancy, lactation, elderly. Renal and hepatic impairment. Increase in onset time in conditions associated with prolonged circulation time (e.g. CV disease, edema). Neuromuscular disease e.g. myasthenia gravis, Eaton-Lambert syndrome or after poliomyelitis. Hypothermia, burns patients. Decrease dose in obese patients, taking into account lean body-mass. Correct severe electrolyte disturbances, altered blood pH, dehydration where possible before vecuronium admin. Do not use potentially dangerous machinery or drive a car within 24 hr after full recovery from the neuromuscular blocking action of vecuronium. Do not admin vecuronium unless facilities for intubation, artificial respiration, oxygen therapy and agents for neuromuscular reversal are immediately available.

British National Formulary 86, 2023

  • Ulcerative colitis (under expert supervision)
    • Adult, by subcutaneous injection, maintenance 108 mg every 2 weeks, following at least 2 intravenous infusions; the first subcutaneous dose should be administered in place of the next scheduled intravenous dose.
  • Crohn's disease (under expert supervision)

drugs.notes:
British National Formulary 84, 2022

  • Monotherapy for the treatment of BRAF V600 mutation-positive unresectable or metastatic melanoma
    • Adult, 960 mg twice daily, for dose adjustment due to side effects.
  • Swallow this medicine whole. Do not chew or crush.
  • Manufacturer advises may be taken with or without food; avoid consistent intake of both daily doses on an empty stomach (may affect absorption).
  • Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) has been reported in patients taking vemurafenib. DRESS syndrome starts with rash, fever, swollen glands, and increased white cell count, and it can affect the liver, kidneys and lungs; DRESS can also be fatal.
  • Effective contraception required during for at least 6 months after treatment.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • This medication makes you more sensitive to sunlight, even when exposed through glass or cloud cover.
  • Avoid sun exposure; wear protective clothing and use a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or SPF 50+ sunscreen.
  • Do not use sunlamps or tanning beds.
  • Tell your doctor if you notice any changes to your skin or problems with your eyes or eyesight.
  • This medicine may increase the effects of caffeine; you may need to reduce your caffeine intake.

drugs.indications: Indicated in combination with azacitidine, or decitabine, or low dose cytarabine for the treatment of newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults 75 years or older, or who have comorbidities that preclude use of intensive induction chemotherapy.
drugs.prescribingRestrictions: To be prescribed by Consultant Hematologist only.
drugs.dosages: The recommended dosage and ramp-up of venetoclax depends on the combination agent. Follow the dosing schedule, including the 3-day or 4-day dose ramp-up, as following: Day 1: 100 mg, Day 2: 200 mg, Day 3: 400 mg, Day 4 and beyond: 400 mg orally once daily of each 28-day cycle in combination with azacitidine or decitabine OR 600 mg orally once daily of each 28-day cycle in combination with low-dose cytarabine. Continue venetoclax, in combination with azacitidine or decitabine or low-dose cytarabine until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
drugs.adverseReactions: Thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, anemia, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, stomatitis, fatigue, asthenia, sepsis, decreased appetite, arthralgia, dizziness/syncope, dyspnea, hemorrhage, hypotension, abdominal pain, pneumonia, weight decreased, hypokalemia, tumor lysis syndrome, headache.
drugs.contraindications: In patients with CLL, concomitant use of venetoclax with strong CYP3A inhibitors is contraindicated at initiation and during ramp-up phase
drugs.interactions: Ketoconazole, ritonavir, posaconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, ciprofloxacin, diltiazem, erythromycin, dronedarone, fluconazole, verapamil, rifampicin, amiodarone, captopril, carvedilol, cyclosporine, felodipine, quercetin, quinidine, ranolazine, ticagrelor, carbamazepine, phenytoin, bosentan, efavirenz, etravirine, modafinil, nafcillin, warfarin, digoxin, everolimus, sirolimus, St. John’s wort, grapefruit, Seville orange, and starfruit.
drugs.precautions: Tumor lysis syndrome, neutropenia, serious infection, immunization
drugs.notes:
British National Formulary 86, 2023

  • Chronic lymphocytic leukemia; Acute myeloid leukemia
    • Adult, specialist drug - access specialist resources for dosing information.
  • If a dose is more than 8 hours late, the missed dose should not be taken and the next dose should be taken at the normal time.
  • Patients should be advised to drink 1.5-2 L of water daily, starting 2 days before and throughout the dose-titration phase; intravenous fluids should be administered for those who cannot maintain an adequate level of oral hydration with consideration of overall risk of tumour lysis syndrome.
  • The MHRA reminds healthcare professionals about the risk of tumour lysis syndrome (TLS) associated with venetoclax, with fatal cases reported, some in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL) receiving the lowest dose (a single dose of venetoclax 20 mg) used in the dose-titration phase and in patients with low-to-medium TLS risk.
  • If vomiting occurs following dose administration, no additional doses should be taken on that day and the next dose should be taken at the normal time.
  • Patients and carers should be counselled on the effects on driving and performance of skilled tasks - increased risk of dizziness and fatigue.
  • Manufacturer advises avoid Seville (bitter orange) and star fruit as they might increase the exposure to venetoclax.
  • Manufacturer advises ensure effective, non-hormonal contraception during and for 30 days after treatment in women of child-bearing potential.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Take with food.
  • This medicine may increase your chances of getting an infection. Contact your doctor immediately if you develop a fever (temperature of 38°C or more) or any other signs of infection.
  • This medicine interacts with many other drugs; ask your doctor or pharmacist before using any other medicines including herbal (particularly St John's wort) and over-the-counter products.
  • Avoid grapefruit juice as it may increase the risk of side effects with venetoclax.

British National Formulary 82, 2021

  • Hypertension

  • Angina
    • Adult, 240 mg twice daily, may sometimes be reduced to once daily.
  • Prophylaxis after myocardial infarction where beta-blockers not appropriate
    • Adult, 360 mg daily in divided doses, started at least 1 week after infarction, given as either 240 mg in the morning and 120 mg in the evening or 120 mg 3 times daily.
  • Calcium-channel blockers differ in their predilection for the various possible sites of action and, therefore, their therapeutic effects are disparate, with much greater variation than those of beta-blockers. There are important differences between verapamil hydrochloride, diltiazem hydrochloride, and the dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers (amlodipine, felodipine, lacidipine, lercanidipine hydrochloride, nicardipine hydrochloride, nifedipine, and nimodipine). It is a highly negatively inotropic calcium channel-blocker and it reduces cardiac output, slows the heart rate, and may impair atrioventricular conduction. It may precipitate heart failure, exacerbate conduction disorders, and cause hypotension at high doses and should not be used with beta-blockers. Constipation is the most common side-effect.

  • Verapamil may increase the effects of alcohol so that you are more easily affected and the effects last longer. Limit your alcohol intake until you know whether you are affected like this.
  • Avoid grapefruit juice as it may increase the risk of side effects with verapamil.

drugs.interactions: Low potential for interactions with co-administered medicinal products. drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Type 2 diabetes
    • Adult, 50 mg twice daily.
    • CrCl <60 ml/min, 50 mg once daily.
    • With metformin, pioglitazone or insulin, 50 mg once or twice daily.
    • With a sulfonylurea, 50 mg once daily.
    • With metformin and sulfonylurea, 50 mg twice daily.
  • Once daily dosing: take in the morning.
  • This medicine can be taken with or without food.
  • DPP-4 inhibitors appear to be less effective in reducing HbA1c than metformin, sulfonylureas or thiazolidinediones.
  • Direct comparative data between the DPP-4 inhibitors are lacking but they all seem to have similar efficacy in reducing HbA1c.
  • All are given once daily except vildagliptin (given once or twice daily).
  • Renal impairment reduces the excretion of alogliptin, sitagliptin and saxagliptin and dose reduction is required; linagliptin is mostly excreted unchanged in the bile (does not need dose adjustment). Although vildagliptin is primarily hepatically metabolised, dose adjustment may be required in renal impairment.

drugs.indications: Hodgkin's disease, choriocarcinoma resistant to other chemotherapeutic agents, non-small cell lung cancer, Langerhans cell histiocytosis
drugs.dosages: Adult, initially, 3.7 mg/m2, increase dose weekly based on WBC counts in increments of about 1.8 mg/m2 until leukocyte count decreases to about 3000/mm3, or maximum weekly dose of 18.5 mg/m2 reached. Usual dose: 5.5-7.4 mg/m2 per week. Do not administer next dose, even though 7 days have lapsed unless the leukocyte count has returned to at least 4000/mm3. Child, initial 2.5 mg/m2 of BSA, increased dose at weekly intervals in increments of about 1.25 mg/m2 until leukocyte count decreases to about 3000/mm3, or maximum weekly dose of 12.5 mg/m2 reached. Do not increase dose once leukocyte count reaches approximately 3000 cells/mm3, instead, a dose of 1 increment smaller to be admin at wkly intervals for maintenance. Do not administer next dose, even though 7 days have lapsed unless the leukocyte count has returned to at least 4000/mm3.
drugs.adverseReactions: Myelosuppression, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, generalized fatigue, constipation, alopecia, dermatitis, vesicant, neurotoxicity, syndrome of inappropriate secretion of anti-diuretic hormone
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to vinblastine. Pregnancy, lactation. Leukopenia, presence of bacterial infection
drugs.interactions: Mitomycin C, phenytoin. Drugs which inhibit cytochrome P450 enzymes, voriconazole, itraconazole. Bone marrow suppressant drug such as azathioprine, interferon, zidovudine, amphotericin B, chloramphenicol.
drugs.precautions: Intrathecal administration can be fatal. Should not be injected into an extremity with impaired circulation. Patients carefully monitored for infection until white cell count has return to normal levels if leukopenia with less than 2000 white blood cells per mm3 occurs following dose
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Tell your doctor or nurse immediately if you feel any pain, stinging or burning during the infusion.
  • Myelosuppression is common and major dose-limiting effect for vinblastine, vinflunine and vinorelbine; significant myelosuppression with vincristine is rare. Mainly affects neutrophils with the nadir occurring about 5-10 days after a dose and recovery after a further 7-14 days. Thrombocytopenia and anemia are less frequent.
  • Neurotoxicity is common and major dose-limiting effect for vincristine; occurs less frequently with vinblastine, vinflunine and vinorelbine; related to both cumulative and individual doses. Includes peripheral neuropathy (e.g. loss of deep tendon reflexes, paresthesia, paralysis) and autonomic neuropathy (e.g. constipation, abdominal pain, paralytic ileus, urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension). Motor function impairment may occur if severe. Vestibular and auditory nerve damage may result in dizziness, nystagmus, vertigo or deafness (may be temporary or permanent). Other adverse effects related to neurotoxicity may include malaise, weakness, headache, depression, jaw pain, ataxia, hoarseness, cortical blindness, seizures, SIADH.
  • Tell your doctor if you become constipated, have unusual bruising or bleeding or if you notice numbness or tingling of your fingers or toes.

British National Formulary 81, 2021

  • Vinblastine is for intravenous administration only. Inadvertent intrathecal administration can cause severe neurotoxicity, which is usually fatal. The National Patient Safety Agency has advised (August 2008) that adult and teenage patients treated in an adult or adolescent unit should receive their vinca alkaloid dose in a 50 ml minibag. Teenagers and children treated in a child unit may receive their vinca alkaloid dose in a syringe.

Product website, accessed 2020 - Kordel's

  • Vitex agnus castus, also known as Chasteberry, has earned the ancient reputation approved by German Commisson E as a gentle and safe herbal remedy.     • Take 1-2 capsules daily, preferable morning before breakfast, or as directed by your healthcare professional.

The Review of Natural Products, 2020

  • Chaste tree extract has been used to manage symptoms related to premenstrual syndrome (PMS) and cyclic mastalgia and may be a suitable alternative to standard pharmacological management. Although the Complete German Commission E Monographs supports its use for PMS and cyclic mastalgia, there are limited clinical trials to support these uses.   • Information regarding safety and efficacy in pregnancy and lactation is lacking. However, chaste tree may have estrogenic, progesterogenic, and/or uterine stimulant activity and should be avoided in pregnancy and while breast-feeding.

drugs.notes:
Martindale The Complete Drug Reference, 2020

  • Vonoprazan is a potassium-competitive acid blocker which competitively inhibits the binding of potassium ions to the enzyme system of hydrogen/potassium adenosine triphosphatase (H+/K+ATPase), the `proton pump' of the gastric parietal cell. It has a rapid onset of action and accumulates in parietal cells giving sustained and potent acid-inhibitory effects over a 24-hour period. It is used in conditions where inhibition of gastric acid secretion may be beneficial, including gastro-esophageal reflux disease, and peptic ulcer disease. It is given as the fumarate but doses are expressed in terms of the base. Vonoprazan fumarate 1.3 mg is equivalent to about 1 mg of vonoprazan.
  • The usual dose for the treatment of gastro-esophageal reflux disease is 20 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks, followed by a further 4 weeks if needed. Maintenance therapy for esophagitis is 10 mg once daily, increased to 20 mg once daily, if needed.
  • In the management of peptic ulcer disease, a dose of 20 mg orally once daily is given for 8 weeks in gastric ulcer and for 6 weeks in duodenal ulcer.
  • Oral doses of 10 mg daily are used in the prevention of NSAID-associated ulceration, including that occurring during low-dose aspirin treatment.
  • For the eradication of Helicobacter pylori in peptic ulceration, oral vonoprazan may be combined with antibacterials in triple therapy. Regimens include vonoprazan 20 mg twice daily combined with amoxicillin 750 mg and clarithromycin 200 mg both given twice daily, or with amoxicillin 750 mg and metronidazole 250 mg both given twice daily. These regimens are given for 7 days.

drugs.indications:
i) Treatment of immunocompromised patients with progressive, possibly life-threatening infections such as invasive aspergillosis, fluconazole-resistant serious invasive candidiasis, serious fungal infections caused by Scedosporium species and Fusarium species
ii) Prevention of breakthrough fungal infections in febrile high-risk neutropenic patients
drugs.dosages: Adult and children 12 years and greater, loading dose: 6 mg/kg 12 hourly for first 24 hours. Maintenance: i) 4 mg/kg 12 hourly; ii) 3 mg/kg 12 hourly. Dose may be increased to 4 mg/kg 12 hourly if response is inadequate. Children aged 2 years to <12 years with normal hepatic and renal function, no loading dose needed; 7 mg/kg 12 hourly.
drugs.adverseReactions: Peripheral edema, rash, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, disease of liver, headache, visual disturbance, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, anaphylactoid reaction, renal failure, jaundice, blood dyscrasias
drugs.contraindications: Co-administration of terfenadine, astemizole, quinidine, sirolimus, rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenobarbitone, efavirenz, ergotamine, dihydroergotamine
drugs.interactions: Alprazolam, bromazepam, clarithromycin, clonazepam, cyclosporine, diazepam, phenytoin, tacrolimus, warfarin, sulfonylureas, statins, benzodiazepines, omeprazole, HIV protease inhibitors, non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, other CYP2C9 or CYP3A4 substrates
drugs.precautions: Electrolyte disturbance, cardiomyopathy, bradycardia, symptomatic arrhythmias, history of QT interval prolongation. Avoid exposure to sunlight, monitor liver function before treatment and during treatment, hematological malignancy, pregnancy (ensure effective contraception during treatment)
drugs.notes:
Frank Shann Drug Doses, 2017

  • Oral: <40 kg liquid 9 mg/kg 12H; ≥40 kg load 400 mg 12H x 2 doses, then 200-300 mg 12H.
  • IV (max 3 mg/kg/hr): load 9 mg/kg (<40 kg) 6 mg/kg (≥40 kg) 12 H x 2 doses, then 8 mg/kg (40 kg) 3-4 mg/kg (≥40 kg) 12H.
  • Beware interactions. Trough level 1-5 mg/L (3-16 µmol/L).

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Invasive aspergillosis and serious infections due to susceptible fungi
    • Adult; child >12 years and >50 kg
      • Loading: IV, 6 mg/kg every 12 hours for 2 doses.
      • Maintenance: IV, 3-4 mg/kg every 12 hours. With phenytoin, IV 5 mg/kg every 12 hours.
    • Child 12-15 years and <50 kg; child 2-12 years
      • Loading: IV, 9 mg/kg every 12 hours for 2 doses.
      • Maintenance: IV, initially 8 mg/kg twice daily; adjust dose in 1 mg/kg steps.
  • Your vision may be blurred and you may be unable to tolerate bright light while taking voriconazole. Do not drive (especially at night) or operate machinery if you are affected.
  • This medicine interacts with many drugs; tell your doctor and pharmacist that you are taking this medicine before starting or stopping any medicines, including herbal and over-the-counter products.

British National Formulary 90, 2025

  • Patients and their carers should be told how to recognise symptoms of liver disorder, and advised to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms such as persistent nausea, vomiting, malaise or jaundice develop.
  • Patients and their carers should be advised that patients should avoid exposure to direct sunlight, and to avoid the use of sunbeds. In sunlight, patients should cover sun-exposed areas of skin and use a sunscreen with a high sun protection factor. Patients should seek medical attention if they experience sunburn or a severe skin reaction following exposure to light or sun.

Lexidrug, 2025

  • Voriconazole may cause visual disturbance, including blurred vision, optic neuritis, vision colour changes, episcleritis and scleritis. Visual disturbances may resolve within 24 hours to 2 weeks after discontinuation. Voriconazole may also cause audio or visual hallucination which may last up to 5 days and are reversible with discontinuation.
  • Peripheral neuropathy has also been reported with numbness or tingling in extremities, which may be rapidly debilitating and irreversible. Encephalopathy has also been reported.
  • Azole antifungals, including voriconazole, may cause hepatotoxicity (ranging from mild, asymptomatic increased serum transaminases to hepatic failure) in adult and pediatric patients.
  • Skin photosensitivity has been reported, including erythematous rashes in sun-exposed areas, bullous phototoxicity and pseudoporphyria in all ages; a higher frequency of phototoxic reactions has been reported in pediatric patients. Photosensitivity may persist for several months after discontinuation of voriconazole. Rare cases of skin malignancy (malignant melanoma, squamous cell carcinoma [SCC]), cutaneous SCC in situ have also been reported in adult and pediatric patients. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs), including toxic epidermal necrolysis and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), have been reported. Alopecia has also been reported.
  • Azole antifungals, including voriconazole, have been associated with prolonged QT interval on ECG, which may lead to torsades de pointes (TdP) or polymorphic ventricular arrhythmias, in both adult and pediatric patients. Numerous cases have been reported with voriconazole, some of which have occurred independently of drug concentrations.

drugs.adverseReactions: Nausea, decreased appetite, abnormal dreams, dizziness, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, generalized pruritus.
drugs.contraindications:
- Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients.
- Concomitant use with non-selective monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) or selective MAO-A inhibitors.
drugs.interactions:
- Irreversible nonselective MAOIs.
- Reversible & selective MAO-A inhibitor e.g., moclobemide.
- Reversible & nonselective MAOI e.g., linezolid.
- Irreversible, selective MAO-B inhibitor e.g., selegiline, rasagiline.
- Serotonergic drugs.
- St. John's wort.
- Higher incidence of adverse reactions w/ bupropion.
- Decreased AUC w/ rifampicin.
- Increased risk of bleeding by oral anticoagulants or antiplatelets.
- Enhanced effects w/ lithium or tryptophan.
drugs.precautions: Suicide/suicidal thoughts or clinical worsening, seizures, serotonin syndrome or neuroleptic malignant syndrome, mania/hypomania, hemorrhage, hyponatremia, renal Impairment, hepatic impairment, elderly & pediatric populations, pregnancy & lactation.
drugs.notes:
British National Formulary 88, 2024

  • Major depression
    • Adult, initially 10 mg once daily; adjusted according to response to 5-20 mg once daily.
    • Elderly, initially 5 mg once daily; increased if necessary up to 20 mg once daily.
  • Manufacturer advises discontinue treatment in patients who develop seizures or if there is an increase in seizure frequency.
  • If used during the later stages of pregnancy, there is a risk of neonatal withdrawal symptoms and persistent pulmonary hypertension in the newborn.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • You may feel dizzy when taking this medicine; be careful driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you.
  • Increased suicidal thoughts and behaviour can occur soon after starting antidepressants, particularly in young people; monitor patients frequently and carefully early in treatment
  • Safety and efficacy data are limited, particularly in the elderly.
  • Vortioxetine can be stopped without tapering the dose.

The Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry, 2021

  • Vortioxetine may be of particular interest owing to its additional benefits on cognition (independent of effects on depressive symptoms).

Product leaflet, accessed 2025 - Brintellix 20 mg/ml Oral Solution Drop

  • Method of administration
    • The oral drops can be taken with or without food.
    • The drops can be mixed with water, juice or other non-alcoholic drinks.
    • The bottle must be turned completely upside down. If no drops come out, the bottle can be tapped lightly to start the flow.
  • Do not store above 30°C.
  • After opening, the drops should be used within 8 weeks.

drugs.indications: Treatment and prophylaxis of thromboembolic disorders
drugs.dosages: Initially 2 to 5 mg per day. Maintenance dose 2-10 mg daily according to the INR. Dosing is individualized based on patient’s INR and according product insert/protocol/ guideline.
drugs.adverseReactions: Hemorrhage, alopecia, fever, gastrointestinal disorders, hypersensitivity reactions, `purple toes'. Occasionally skin necrosis (obese elderly patients), jaundice, hepatic dysfunction, nausea, vomiting, pancreatitis. NPRA Safety Alert (6 May 2022): Anticoagulant-related nephropathy.
drugs.contraindications: Hemorrhagic tendencies, pregnancy, blood dyscrasias, hypersensitivity to warfarin products
drugs.interactions: Activity potentiated by cimetidine, clofibrate, co-trimoxazole, erythromycin, quinidine, phenylbutazone, sulphonamides, amiodarone, rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, azole antifungals, metronidazole. Drugs which may increase risk of bleeding including aspirin, NSAIDs, dipyridamole, clopidogrel, ticlopidine
drugs.precautions: Severe to moderate hepatic or renal insufficiency, concomitant use of antiplatelet drugs or drugs with ulcerogenic activity. Surgery and dental extraction, congestive heart failure. Concurrent use with thrombolytic drugs, known or suspected protein C deficiency. Moderate to severe hypertension, severe diabetes, severe allergic or anaphylactic disorders. Patients with hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism may have a substantially altered response to warfarin. Avoid concurrent use with herbal medicines and limit Vitamin K rich vegetables. NPRA Safety Alert (6 May 2022): Anticoagulant-related nephropathy - patients with altered glomerular integrity or with a history of kidney disease. NPRA Safety Alert (22 Aug 2025): Risk of Atraumatic Splenic Rupture.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Always take the same brand of tablets.
  • Take tablets at about the same time every day. Record your dose and when you take the tablets, as well as your INR results, using a calendar or 'anticoagulant book'.
  • You need regular blood tests (INR) with this medicine; call for the result within 24 hours of the test and before the next dose, in case it needs adjusting. Tell your doctor if you have missed doses or if you have any other illness, including diarrhea, vomiting, infection or fever; extra blood tests may be needed.
  • Warfarin is affected by vitamin K, which is found in certain foods. Eat a normal, balanced diet (including green vegetables) without varying it too much, to keep your intake of vitamin K stable.
  • Avoid excessive alcohol consumption; 1-2 standard drinks daily is generally safe.
  • Avoid drinking large amounts of cranberry juice as this may increase the effects of warfarin.
  • Tell your doctor and pharmacist that you are taking this medicine before starting or stopping any other medication or taking vitamin supplements, herbal or over-the-counter products.
  • Tell your dentist, podiatrist, physiotherapist or chiropractor that you are taking this medicine.
  • Tell your doctor immediately if you have any unexplained bruising, bleeding, pink, red or dark brown urine, or red or black feces.
  • Tell your doctor if you develop a painful, purplish, bruise-like rash.

Sarawak Handbook of Medical Emergencies, 2019

  • Patient with large anterior MI should be considered for treatment with warfarin/DOACs for 3-6 months.
  • Patients with severe LV dysfunction, AF or left ventricular aneurysm should be treated with warfarin/DOACs long-term to decrease the risk of systemic embolization.
  • Anticoagulation with warfarin or direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) reduce risk of systemic embolization by almost 70% and should be considered for most AF patients.
  • The evidence does not support the use of antiplatelet agents for the prevention of thromboembolic events in AF. They are mainly used in patients who cannot take anticoagulation therapy for reasons other than bleeding risk.

drugs.notes:
Australian Injectable Drugs Handbook, 2020

  • Tonicity: hypotonic.
  • Reconstituting medicines that are formulated as a powder or diluting medicines before injection.
  • Not suitable for fluid replacement as it causes hemolysis of blood cells.

ACCP Updates in Therapeutics, 2021

  • Sterile water alone should never be administered intravenously (avoid using intravenous fluid with an osmolality less than 150 mOsm/L).
  • In reality, a patient with mild hypernatremia generally needs water, not additional Na+. Therefore, for patients with hypernatremia, enteral administration of water is preferable. If the enteral route is unavailable, recommend D5W administered intravenously.

Product leaflet, accessed 2024

  • One vial (10 ml) of Soluvit N contains thiamine mononitrate 3.1 mg (corresponding to vitamin B1 2.5 mg), riboflavin sodium phosphate 4.9 mg (corresponding to vitamin B2 3.6 mg), nicotinamide 40 mg, pyridoxine hydrochloride 4.9 mg (corresponding to vitamin B6 4.0 mg), sodium pantothenate 16.5 mg (corresponding to pantothenic acid 15.0 mg), sodium ascorbate 113 mg (corresponding to vitamin C 100 mg), biotin 60 µg, folic acid 0.40 mg and cyanocobalamin 5.0 µg.
  • Osmolality in 10 ml of water approximately 490 mosm/kg water.
  • Soluvit N is indicated in adult patients and children as a supplement in intravenous nutrition to meet the daily requirements of watersoluble vitamins.
    • For adult patients and children weighing 10 kg or more, the recommended daily dosage is the content of one vial.
    • Infants and children weighing less than 10 kg should be given 1 ml of the dissolved mixture per kg body weight per day.
  • Soluvit N must not be given undiluted. The contents of one vial are dissolved by adding 10 ml of:
    • Vitalipid N Infant (for children above 10 kg/bw); or
    • Intralipid 10%, Intralipid 20%; or
    • Water for Injections; or
    • Glucose solution for infusion (5%-50%)
  • When Soluvit N is diluted with water-based solutions, the admixture should be protected from light.
    • This is not necessary if Soluvit N is diluted with Intralipid because of the protective effect of the fat emulsion.
  • Chemical and physical in-use stability after dilution has been demonstrated for 24 hours at 25°C. From a microbiological point of view, the product should be used immediately. If not used immediately, in-use storage times and conditions prior to use are the responsibility of the user and would normally not be longer than 24 hours at 2-8°C, unless mixing has taken place in controlled and validated aseptic conditions.

Product leaflet, accessed 2024

  • Each 5 ml contains Folium Artemisiae Argyi 0.09 mg, Flos Caryophylli 0.05 mg, Radix Glycyrrhizae 0.035 mg, Semen Armeniacae 0.035 mg, Sanguis Draconis 0.1 mg, Tea Tree Oil 0.04 ml, Oleum Cinnamomi 0.05 ml, Peppermint Oil 0.9 ml, Paraffin Oil 3.7 ml.
  • Used traditionally to relieve the symptoms of colds, headaches and insect bites, abdominal pain and bloating.
    • Apply 2-4 drops on a sore body 3-4 times a day or as needed.

Australian Pharmaceutical Formulary and Handbook 23, 2015

  • Wound closure strips are specialized narrow tapes used for simple skin tears and lacerations that have no exudate, and to reinforce loosely sutured wounds. They can act like sutures in first aid situations. The strips are applied at right angles to the wound, 3-5 mm apart. Wound edges should be gently pushed together, while lightly pressing down on the strip. The strips should not be overstretched. Skin-colored and elastic forms are available.

Product leaflet, accessed 2021

  • X-temp Oral Suspension contains specialized suspending system formulated to assist in extemporaneous preparation of oral liquid, non-soluble (suspended), aqueous dosage forms. It is orange flavored, sweetened, sugar-free vehicle containing suitable preservatives.
  • X-temp Oral Suspension is buffered and pH balanced to provide maximum flexibility which is convenient, consistent and predictable for preparation of pediatric and geriatric medications administered orally. Medicated powders and crushed tablets can be compounded into X-temp Oral Suspension to provide smooth, elegant, uniform and physically stable suspensions.
  • Store below 30°C. Protect from direct sunlight, heat and moisture. Keep out of reach of children.
  • Suggested use: Shake well before use.

drugs.genericName: Xuezhikang (Standardized Red Yeast Rice Extract Concentrate) 600 mg Capsule
drugs.notes:
MIMS, 2021

  • Reducing elevated levels of serum total-C, LDL-C & TG; increasing HDL-C in individuals with moderate primary dyslipidaemia.
    • Adult, 1 capsule BD.
  • Should be taken with food.

The Review of Natural Products, 2021

  • Monascus purpureus is a natural source of lovastatin, used in the treatment of hyperlipidemia. The compound is usually referred to as "monacolin K" or "mevinolin" when discussing red yeast rice or other natural sources. Red yeast rice may have a role in managing dyslipidemia, especially when statin intolerance has resulted in poor concordance with pharmaceutical interventions. Traditional red yeast rice often contains very low levels of monacolin K, while more modern preparations may contain levels approaching prescription dosage levels; neither should be used without clinical oversight. Studies have been conducted to evaluate its antibacterial, antioxidant, and CNS effects, as well as its activity on glycemic metabolism, but quality clinical trials are lacking to recommend use for these indications.
  • Red yeast rice is available commercially, primarily in 600 mg capsules. Most manufacturers suggest an oral dosage of 2 capsules twice a day for a total dose of 2400 mg/day. Clinical trials evaluating the safety and efficacy of red yeast rice compared to statins or placebo for improvement of lipid profiles reported dosages of 1200 to 3600 mg/day for durations of 4 to 12 weeks.
  • Studies in rodents and limited case reports have raised concerns regarding decreases in coenzyme Q10 and development of myopathy due to red yeast rice. However, a meta-analysis of 53 clinical trials (N=8,535) published up to February 2019 found no increased risk of musculoskeletal adverse effects for red yeast rice versus comparator; this result was similar to that of an earlier meta-analysis of 20 clinical trials conducted up to 2014. Reports of adulteration with prescription lovastatin exist, which may account for some observed adverse effects. Evidence regarding supplementation with oral coenzyme Q10 to increase mitochondrial levels is equivocal.
  • Avoid use during pregnancy and lactation. One ingredient in red yeast rice is monacolin K, also known as mevinolin or lovastatin; based on theoretical considerations and small case studies, statins are potential teratogens. CNS and limb defects have been reported in newborns exposed to statins in utero.

drugs.notes:
MIMS, 2021

  • Otrivin 0.05% nasal drops
    • Children 1-5 years old, 1-2 drops into each nostril once or twice daily (every 8 to 10 hours) are generally sufficient. Do not exceed 3 applications daily into each nostril.
    • Children 6-11 years old, 2-4 drops into each nostril, 2 to 3 times daily as needed. Do not exceed 3 applications daily into each nostril.
    • Should not be used in children aged less than 1 year old.
  • Otirivin 0.1% nasal spray
    • Adults and adolescents over 12 years, 1-2 sprays into each nostril, up to 3 times daily as needed. Do not exceed 3 applications daily into each nostril.
    • Should not be used in children aged less than 12 years old.

drugs.indications:
To reduce the rate of maternal-fetal transmission of HIV in:
i) HIV-positive pregnant women over 14 weeks of gestation
ii) Their newborn infants
drugs.dosages:
i) Prophylaxis of maternal-fetal HIV transmission during labor and delivery: Adult, loading dose: 2 mg/kg, followed by continuous infusion of 1 mg/kg/hr until umbilical cord is clamped. If caesarean section is planned, start the IV infusion 4 hr before the operation. renal and Hepatic impairment, dose reduction may be needed.
HIV infection (to be discuss: not in indication) Adult, 1-2 mg/kg every 4 hr, given as 2-4 mg/ml infusion over 1 hr. Child, as continuous infusion: 20 mg/m2/hr. Alternatively, as intermittent infusion: 120 mg/m2 every 6 hr. Renal impairment, hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis: 1 mg/kg every 6-8 hr.
ii) Prophylaxis of HIV infection in neonates: Neonates, 1.5 mg/kg every 6 hr. Start treatment within 12 hr after birth and continue for 1st 6 wk of life. Dose to be given via IV infusion over 30 minutes. Renal impairment, dose adjustment may be needed.
drugs.adverseReactions: Anemia, neutropenia, leukopenia, nausea, headache, rash, abdominal pain, fever, myalgia, paresthesia, vomiting, insomnia and anorexia. Asthenia, malaise, somnolence, diarrhea, dizziness, sweating, dyspnea, dyspepsia, flatulence, bad taste, chest pain, loss of mental acuity, anxiety, urinary frequency, depression, generalized pain, chills, cough, urticaria, pruritus and flu-like syndrome
drugs.contraindications: Abnormally low neutrophil cell count (less than 0.75 x 109/L) or abnormally low Hb levels (less than 7.5 g/dL). Hypersensitivity to zidovudine. New born infants with hyperbilirubinemia requiring treatment other than phototherapy, or increased transaminase levels of over five times than the upper limit of normal.
drugs.interactions: Increased hematological toxicity with IV pentamidine, lamivudine, dapsone, vancomycin flucytosine, amphotericin, ganciclovir, rifampicin, interferon alfa, cyclophosphamide and other with bone marrow suppressive or cytotoxic agents. Increased risk of zidovudine toxicity with atovaquone, chloramphenicol, fluconazole, valproate. Decreased absorption with clarithromycin. Increased zidovudine concentration and increased potential for hypersensitivity reactions with probenecid. Increased incidences of headache with benzodiazepines Avoid stavudine (due to inhibition of activation of stavudine), didanosine, ribavirin (antagonize effect of zidovudine) with zidovudine.
drugs.precautions: Monitor carefully hematological parameters. If anemia or myelosuppression occurs dose adjustments are suggested. Patients with pre-existing bone marrow compromise. Pregnancy and lactation. Renal and hepatic impairment.
drugs.notes:
Malaysian Consensus Guidelines on Antiretroviral Therapy, 2017

  • Intrapartum IV Zidovudine (AZT) infusion (2 mg/kg for the 1st hour followed by 1 mg/kg/h subsequently) is recommended for women with a viral load of >1000 copies/mL who present in labor or with ruptured membranes or who are admitted for planned PLCS. Current evidence suggests that intrapartum IV AZT has no additional benefit in prevention of vertical transmission in pregnant women on ART with viral load ≤1000 copies/mL during late pregnancy and near delivery.

Australian Medicines Handbook Children's Dosing Companion, 2021

  • Prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV
    • Start as soon after birth as possible, preferably within 4-12 hours. Inclusion of other antiretrovirals depends on the estimated risk of mother-to-child transmission.
    • Preterm neonate, IV 1.5 mg/kg twice daily for 4 weeks.
    • Term neonate, IV 1.5 mg/kg 4 times daily for 4 weeks.

    • >34 weeks gestation, 4 mg/kg twice daily for 4 weeks.

Malaysian Consensus Guidelines on Antiretroviral Therapy, 2017

  • Discontinue zidovudine if Hb has dropped ≥25% of baseline or <8.0 g/dL or when patient develops symptomatic anemia and/or leukopenia.

  • Tell your doctor if you have extreme tiredness, weakness, pale skin, bleeding, sore throat or infection.

  • Lactic acidosis associated with hepatomegaly and hepatic steatosis has been reported with zidovudine. Use with caution in patients with hepatomegaly, hepatitis, or other risk factors for liver disease and hepatic steatosis (including obesity and alcohol abuse). Manufacturer advises discontinue treatment if symptoms of hyperlactatemia, lactic acidosis, progressive hepatomegaly or rapid deterioration of liver function become apparent.
  • Lipodystrophy syndrome: Metabolic effects may occur with zidovudine; plasma lipids and blood glucose concentrations should be measured routinely.

drugs.genericName: Zolbetuximab 100 mg/vial Powder for Concentrate for Solution for Infusion
drugs.notes:
Lexidrug, 2025

  • Gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic, HER2 negative, CLDN18.2 positive
    • Adult, initial dose: IV: 800 mg/m2 on cycle 1, day 1 (in combination with either oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, and leucovorin [mFOLFOX regimen] or oxaliplatin and capecitabine [CAPOX regimen]).
    • Adult, subsequent doses: IV: 600 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks or 400 mg/m2 once every 2 weeks; in combination with either a total of 4 cycles (each cycle is 42 days) of mFOLFOX or a total of 8 cycles of CAPOX, followed by zolbetuximab and either fluorouracil/leucovorin or capecitabine until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
  • Zolbetuximab is associated with a high emetic potential; provide antiemetic prophylaxis with an NK-1 receptor antagonist, a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist, and other antiemetics to prevent nausea and vomiting.
  • For IV infusion only; do not administer as IV push or bolus. Inline filters (pore size 0.2 micron) are recommended during infusion.
  • Store intact vials at 2°C to 8°C (36°F to 46°F); do not freeze. Store in the original carton. Do not shake.

drugs.indications:
i) Treatment of hypercalcemia of malignancy
ii) Prevention of skeletal related events (SREs) in patients with multiple myeloma involving multiple bone lesions
iii) Prevention of skeletal related events (SREs) for metastatic cancers of solid tumors
drugs.dosages:
i) 4 mg single dose
ii) 4 mg every 3-4 weeks
iii) 4 mg reconstituted and should be given as a 15-minute IV infusion every 12 weeks (as advised in MaHTAS 2018 Report)
drugs.adverseReactions: Anemia, headache, paresthesia, sleep disorder, conjunctivitis, nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, hyperhidrosis, bone pain, myalgia, arthralgia, generalized body pain, joint stiffness, hypertension, renal impairment, acute phase reaction, pyrexia, influenza-like illness (including: fatigue, chills, malaise, and flushing), peripheral edema, asthenia, hypophosphatemia, blood creatinine and blood urea increased, hypocalcemia.
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to zoledronic acid or other bisphosphonates, pregnancy, lactation
drugs.interactions: Aminoglycosides, calcitonin, loop diuretics, other potentially nephrotoxic drugs, anti-angiogenic drugs
drugs.precautions: Inadequate hydration, concomitant administration with other bisphosphonates, deterioration of renal function, severe renal impairment (not recommended), severe hepatic impairment, atypical fractures of the femur, musculoskeletal pain, osteonecrosis, concomitant administration with other hypocalcemia causing drugs.
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Ensure patient is adequately hydrated before use for any indication; in hypercalcemia, restore and maintain adequate hydration with IV sodium chloride 0.9%
  • Monitor plasma concentrations of calcium, phosphate and magnesium during treatment.
  • Measure serum creatinine before each dose; if renal function deteriorates, withhold further dosing until serum creatinine returns to within 10% of baseline value unless there is life-threatening hypercalcemia; restart at the same dose given before treatment interruption.
  • Calcium and vitamin D supplements:
    • Consider for patients with advanced bone malignancies or osteoporosis.
    • In Paget's disease, ensure adequate vitamin D intake and give calcium supplementation for at least 10 days following zoledronic acid dose, to prevent hypocalcemia.
  • For most Paget's disease patients, biochemical markers of bone turnover remained in the normal range for several years following a single dose of zoledronic acid; information on re-treatment is limited.

ACCP Updates in Therapeutics, 2020

  • Osteonecrosis of jaw: Most are associated with dental procedures. Most cases occur in patients with cancer after prolonged therapy. High-dose intravenous administration (usually for cancer-related issues) has a greater risk than oral therapy.

drugs.indications: For treatment of insomnia
drugs.dosages: Adult, 10 mg daily at bedtime. Elderly or debilitated subjects, 5 mg daily at bed time. Max. dose: 10 mg daily.
drugs.adverseReactions: Nausea, dizziness, dependence, vertigo, headache, drowsiness, myalgias, dyspepsia, dry mouth, lethargy, flu-like symptoms, depression, constipation, ataxia, hallucinations
drugs.contraindications: Obstructive sleep apnea, acute pulmonary insufficiency, respiratory depression, myasthenia gravis, severe hepatic impairment, psychotic illness, pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypersensitivity
drugs.interactions: Alcohol, analgesics, antidepressants, anticoagulants, sedating antihistamines, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, central alpha 2 agonists, ethanol, opiate agonists/antagonists, itraconazole, sertraline, rifampicin, ritonavir, venlafaxine
drugs.precautions: Depression, drug or alcohol abuse, hepatic impairment, avoid prolonged use in elderly, lactation, renal impairment, abrupt discontinuation, central nervous system effects, drowsiness, hallucination
drugs.notes:
Lexicomp, 2021

  • Administer immediately before bedtime due to rapid onset of action. Regardless of dosage form, do not administer with or immediately after a meal (may delay onset).

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • This medication is intended to make you feel sleepy, but you may be less alert or even drowsy the following day. Avoid driving or operating heavy equipment for at least 8 hours after taking your tablet and possibly longer, depending on how you react.
  • Do not take alcohol or other medications that may cause drowsiness while taking zolpidem, as this may increase the risk of walking or driving while you're asleep.
  • Use the lowest possible dose short term only:
    • dependence, tolerance and misuse comparable to benzodiazepines can occur
    • a withdrawal syndrome may occur on stopping, particularly if taking high doses; prevent or alleviate by gradual dose reduction

drugs.dosages: For adults, usually 100 to 200 mg of zonisamide is to be administered orally 1 to 3 times a day initially. The dose is gradually increased at every one to two weeks up to 200-400 mg daily, in 1 to 3 divided dose. The maximum daily dose should not exceed 600 mg per day.
drugs.adverseReactions: Main adverse reactions were sleepiness, anorexia, elevations of γ-GTP, ALP, ALT (GPT) and AST (GOT) etc., enervation and decrease of spontaneity, ataxia, nausea and vomiting, malaise and weakness and decreased mental activity. Other adverse effect: Muco-cutaneous-ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrosis (Lyell's syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, Delayed serious hypersensitivities, Aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis, pure red cell aplasia, thrombocytopenia, acute renal failure, interstitial pneumonia, Hepatic function disorder, jaundice, rhabdomyolysis, renal and urinary tract calculus, heat stroke accompanied with decreased sweating.
drugs.contraindications: Patients with a history of hypersensitivity to zonisamide, sulphonamides or any of ingredients. Lactation.
drugs.interactions: Should be administered with care when co-administered with these drugs: Antiepileptic drugs, phenytoin, carbamazepine sodium valproate, etc.
drugs.precautions: Patients with severe hepatic dysfunction or those with its anamnesis. Since a radical reduction of the dose or an abrupt discontinuance of the administration may cause status epilepticus, while the patients take the drug, the discontinuance should be carefully carried out by reducing the dose gradually. Special attention should be paid to the elderly and debilitated patients. It is recommended that hepatic and renal function tests and blood examinations should be performed regularly during the administration. Not to be engaged in potentially dangerous tasks such as operating machinery or driving vehicles during the drug administration. For more appropriate adjustment of the dosage, it is desirable to measure the blood concentration of this drug. Careful attention should be paid to the rise of body temperature during treatment with zonisamide. Other Precautions: Abnormality of serum immunoglobulin such as IgA and IgG may occur
drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • This medicine may make you feel drowsy or dizzy especially when you start treatment or the dose is increased; if affected, do not drive or operate machinery.
  • Zonisamide may also increase the effects of alcohol.
  • Make sure you drink enough water every day, especially if you have had kidney stones in the past.
  • Zonisamide may reduce or prevent sweating. Tell your doctor if this happens to you as it may affect your body's ability of cool down, especially in hot weather.
  • Tell your doctor immediately if you develop a rash.
  • Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly unless your doctor tells you to.
  • Avoid stopping treatment abruptly; gradually taper daily dose, e.g. by 100 mg each week.
  • Zonisamide weakly inhibits renal carbonic anhydrase, which may lead to a decrease in serum bicarbonate concentrations and rarely to hyperchloraemic, normal anion gap, metabolic acidosis. Chronic untreated metabolic acidosis may increase risk of kidney stones, osteomalacia and osteoporosis.

Rang and Dale's Pharmacology, 2020

  • It is mainly free of major unwanted effects, although it causes drowsiness, and of serious interaction with other drugs.
  • It tends to suppress appetite and cause weight loss, and is sometimes used for this purpose.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Short-term treatment of insomnia
    • Adult, 7.5 mg at night for up to 4 weeks. Reduce to 3.75 mg if possible.
    • Elderly, debilitated, significant respiratory, renal or hepatic impairment, initially 3.75 mg at night.
  • This medication is intended to make you feel sleepy, but you may be less alert or even drowsy the following day, especially in the 12 hours after taking your tablet; avoid driving or operating heavy equipment until you know how you react.
  • Do not take alcohol or other medications that may cause drowsiness while taking zopiclone, as this may increase the risk of walking or driving while you're asleep.
  • Depression, psychosis or schizophrenia may worsen (including risk of suicide). In addition, combining zopiclone with drugs used to treat these conditions may increase the likelihood of complex sleep behaviors, e.g. sleep driving. Drug or alcohol misuse or psychiatric disorders increases the risk of dependence.

drugs.indications: Only for treatment of agitated and violent patients suffering from schizophrenia who are not responding to the available standard drugs
drugs.dosages: Clopixol-Acuphase: Clopixol-Acuphase is administered by IM injection. The dosage range should normally be 50-150 mg (1-3 ml) IM repeated if necessary, preferably with a time interval of 2-3 days. In a few patients, an additional injection may be needed 24-48 hrs following the 1st injection. In the maintenance therapy, treatment should be continued with oral Clopixol or Clopixol Depot IM after the following guidelines: Change to Oral Clopixol: 2-3 days after the last injection of Clopixol-Acuphase, a patient who has been treated with 100 mg Clopixol-Acuphase, oral treatment should be started at a dosage of about 40 mg daily, possibly in divided dosages. If necessary, the dose can be further increased by 10-20 mg every 2-3 days up to 75 mg or more.

drugs.notes:
Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Acute psychoses, acute mania
    • Adult, IM 50-150 mg every 2-3 days, up to 400 mg per course (up to 4 doses); treat for a maximum of 2 weeks before switching to alternative zuclopenthixol formulation (i.e. oral or long-acting injection). Lower doses may be needed in the elderly.
    • Changing to oral, 40 mg daily orally is considered equivalent to an intermediate-acting injection dose of 100 mg every 2-3 days. Give the first oral dose 2-3 days after the last injection.
    • Changing to long-acting injection, give the first long-acting dose with the last intermediate-acting injection.
  • May be useful in highly disturbed patients who are poorly compliant with oral drugs; not recommended in acute psychosis due to organic disorders.
  • Sedation is significant in the first few hours after the first injection, maximal at 12 hours, and may last up to 3 days.

Australian Medicines Handbook, 2021

  • Chronic psychoses
    • Consider giving a 100 mg test dose to patients not previously treated with long-acting antipsychotic injections to check for adverse effects (use a lower dose for frail or elderly patients).
    • Adult, 200-400 mg every 2-4 weeks. Lower doses may be needed in the elderly.
    • Changing from oral, multiply the current oral dose by 8 to obtain the dose of long-acting injection to give every 2 weeks. Continue oral dosing, tapering it during the first week.
    • Changing from intermediate-acting injection, give the first long-acting dose with the last intermediate-acting injection.

drugs.genericName: β-carotene 10000 IU, Vit C 300 mg, Vit E 100 IU, Vit B2 12 mg, Selenium 50 mcg, Zinc 16 mg, Copper 2 mg and Lutein 4 mg (supplying 200 mcg Zeaxanthin) Time Release Tablet
drugs.notes:
MIMS, 2020

  • Each tablet contains β-carotene (provitamin A) 10000 IU, vit C (ascorbic acid) 300 mg, vit E (d-alpha tocopheryl acetate) 100 IU, vit B2(riboflavin) 12 mg, selenium (hydrolyzed vegetable origin chelate) 50 mcg, zinc (gluconate) 16 mg, copper (hydrolyzed vegetable origin chelate) 2 mg and lutein 4 mg (supplying 200 mcg zeaxanthin).
  • Dietary supplement
    • Adult, take 1 tablet daily with a meal.

The Review of Natural Products, 2024

  • There is a lack of consensus and limited evidence from clinical and epidemiological studies regarding whether an association exists between a higher intake of xanthophylls (lutein with or without zeaxanthin) and protection against age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and cataracts. Studies have also evaluated effects of lutein on cardiovascular outcomes. Clinical trial data are lacking to recommend use for any indication.
    • A dose of lutein 5 mg/day is widely accepted. AMD trials have used lutein dosages of 10 to 20 mg/day for varying durations (e.g., 4 to 12 months).
  • No clinically important adverse reactions were reported at lutein doses up to 20 mg/day.
